Lily thought hard. She remembered that she took her yellow color to the park yesterday. She wanted to paint the sun. But she forgot to bring it back. She said, "Oh no, Mom. I left my yellow color in the park. What can I do?"

Mom said, "Don't worry, Lily. We can go to the park and look for it. Maybe it is still there. Or maybe someone found it and gave it to the park man. Come on, let's get ready and go."

Lily was happy. She put on her shoes and coat. She took her box of colors and her paper book. She hoped to find her yellow color. She wanted to finish her flower. She said, "Thank you, Mom. You are the best. Let's go to the park and find my yellow color."

Lily and Ben were hungry. They wanted to eat something yummy. They went to the kitchen and looked in the fridge. They saw a can of tuna. They liked tuna.

"Can we have tuna, please?" Lily asked Ben.

"OK, but we need to ask Mom first," Ben said. He was older and knew the rules.

They ran to the living room, where Mom was reading a book. They tugged on her sleeve and showed her the can of tuna.

"Mom, can we have tuna, please?" they both said.

Mom smiled and put down her book. She looked at the can of tuna. It was rare tuna. It was very good and very expensive. She had bought it for a special occasion.

"Are you sure you want tuna?" she asked. "This is rare tuna. It is not like the tuna you usually have. It is pink and soft and has a different taste."

Lily and Ben nodded. They did not care. They just wanted to eat tuna.

Mom shrugged. She opened the can of tuna and put some on a plate. She gave them some bread and butter and a glass of milk each. She watched them eat.

Lily and Ben took a bite of the rare tuna. They made a face. They did not like it. It was too pink and too soft and too different. They wanted the tuna they usually had. It was white and flaky and familiar.

They pushed the plate away and looked at Mom.

"Mom, we don't like this tuna," they said.

Mom sighed. She had wasted the rare tuna. She should have known better. She urged them to try again.

"Please, give it another chance," she said. "It is very good and very expensive. You might like it if you try again."

Lily and Ben shook their heads. They did not want to try again. They wanted the tuna they usually had.

Mom gave up. She took the plate and the can of tuna. She put them in the fridge. She made them some cheese sandwiches instead. They ate them happily.

Mom decided to save the rare tuna for another day. Maybe Dad would like it. Or maybe she would eat it herself. She hoped it would not go bad. She wondered why she had bought it in the first place.

"Hey, kid, get away from my dog!" the man shouts. "He is not your friend. He is mine!"

Tom is scared. He lets go of the dog and runs to Lily. The man grabs the dog and puts the leash on him. He glares at Tom and Lily.

Tom and Lily nod. They are sorry. They learned a lesson. They will not be foolish again. They will be careful with animals. They will play with their own toys. They will have fun in the park.

From that day on, Rudolph and his friends were very happy because they had prevented a bad thing from happening. They played in the snow and ate some yummy berries. And Rudolph was still very hairy, but his friends loved him just the same. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby little bear named Benny. Benny loved to eat honey and play in the forest with his friends. One day, Benny and his friend Timmy were playing tag when it started to rain. 

Benny said, "Oh no, I don't want to get wet!" 

Timmy replied, "It's okay, we can go under this big tree and stay dry." 

But the rain was too heavy, and soon Benny's fur was soaked. He said, "My fur is all wet, and now my waist feels heavy." 

Timmy said, "Let's go to my house and dry off by the fire." 

So they went to Timmy's house and Benny sat by the fire to dry off. He felt much better and said, "Thank you, Timmy. Now my fur is dry and my waist feels light again."

Lily felt happy that she could help the bird. She learned that sometimes, even small things like throwing a rock can make a big difference. From that day on, Lily always looked for ways to help others.

Tweety thought it was a good idea and they went to find some paint. They saw a big crane painting a building and asked if they could use some of the paint. The crane said yes and gave them some paint.

They painted a picture of seeds and pretended to eat them. But the paint was poisonous and made them sick. They both got very sick and couldn't fly or run anymore. They wished they had never painted the picture.

The moral of the story is: never eat paint, even if you're hungry.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play together. One day, they decide to have a tea party. They find a small table and some cups and a pot. They fill the pot with water and pretend it is tea.

"Would you like some tea, Ben?" Lily asks.

"Yes, please, Lily. Thank you," Ben says.

Lily pours some water into Ben's cup. She pours some water into her cup, too. She picks up her cup and sips it.

"Mmm, this tea is good," she says.

Ben picks up his cup and sips it. He makes a face.

"Yuck, this tea is bad," he says.

Lily looks at Ben. She does not understand.

"Why do you say that, Ben? The tea is good," she says.

Ben shakes his head.

"No, Lily, the tea is bad. It has no sugar. I like sugar in my tea," he says.

Lily thinks for a moment. She remembers that she has some sugar in her kitchen. She gets up and runs to get it.

"Wait here, Ben. I have something for you," she says.

She comes back with a small bowl of sugar. She puts some sugar in Ben's cup and stirs it.

"Here, Ben. Try it now. Maybe you will like it," she says.

Ben sips his tea again. He smiles.

"Mmm, this tea is good," he says.

Lily smiles, too.

"I'm glad you like it, Ben. I like sugar in my tea, too. We both like the same thing," she says.

They sip their tea and talk. They are happy. They understand each other. They are good friends.

Tom and Sue are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a fat man on a bench. He has a lot of money in his hand. He is counting his money.

"Wow, look at that!" Tom says. "He has so much money!"

"Maybe he is rich," Sue says. "Or maybe he is bad. Maybe he took the money from someone else."

Tom and Sue are curious. They want to see the money. They walk closer to the fat man. They try to be quiet.

"Hello, kids," the fat man says. He sees Tom and Sue. He smiles. "Do you like money?"

Tom and Sue nod. They like money. Money can buy toys and candy.

"Would you like some money?" the fat man asks. He holds out a bill. "You can have this if you do something for me."

"What do you want us to do?" Tom asks.

The fat man points to a lady. She is walking her dog. She has a purse on her shoulder.

"See that lady?" the fat man says. "She has more money in her purse. I want you to take her purse and bring it to me. Then I will give you more money. Do you mind?"

Tom and Sue look at each other. They are scared. They know it is wrong to take someone's purse. They do not want to be bad.

"Yes, we mind," Sue says. "We do not want to take her purse. That is not nice. That is stealing."

The fat man frowns. He is angry. He puts his money away.

"Fine, then," he says. "Go away. You are no fun. You are silly kids."

Tom and Sue run away. They do not want to talk to the fat man anymore. They do not like him. He is mean.

They find their mom. She is waiting for them. She hugs them.

"Did you have fun in the park?" she asks.

Mom is proud of them. She says they did the right thing. She says they are good and smart.

She gives them a treat. She gives them some money. She says they can buy something they like.

Tom and Sue are happy. They do not need the fat man's money. They have their mom's money. They have their mom's love. They have each other.

Anna nodded and packed her bear in her backpack. She was ready to go.

"Agent Tom, do you copy?" Amy says into the wire.

"Yes, Agent Amy, I hear you," Tom says.

"Good. We have a mission. We need to find the secret code. It is in a book. The book is on the shelf. But be careful. There are bad guys in the room. They look like ordinary people, but they are not. They are robots."

"OK, Agent Amy. I will be sneaky. You watch for the robots. Over and out."

Tom crawls to the shelf. He looks at the books. He sees one with a star on the cover. He thinks that is the one. He reaches for it. But then he hears a beep.

"Agent Tom, we have a problem. The robots have seen us. They are coming. Run!"

Tom grabs the book and runs to Amy. They drop the wire and run to the door. They open it and see their mom.

"Hi, kids. What are you doing?" she asks.

"We are spies, mom. We have the secret code. We saved the world," Tom says.

"Wow, that sounds fun. But what is this wire?" she asks.

"It is our spy phone, mom. We use it to talk to each other," Amy says.

"That's very clever. But you know you should not play with wires. They can be dangerous. You could get hurt. Why don't you use something else, like a toy phone or a walkie-talkie?" she says.

"OK, mom. We will. But can we keep the book? It has the secret code," Tom says.

"Really? That's cool. Can we do that now?" Amy says.

"OK, mom. We will. Thank you," Tom and Amy say.

Anna loved honey. She liked to eat it on bread, on fruit, on yogurt, and sometimes just with a spoon. She always asked her mom for honey when she was hungry or sad or happy.

One day, Anna and her mom went to the farm. They saw cows, sheep, pigs, and chickens. Anna liked to pet them and feed them. But her favorite thing was to see the bees. The bees lived in a big box with many holes. They flew in and out and made a buzzing sound. Anna wanted to see how they made honey.

"Mom, can I see the honey?" Anna asked.

"Sure, honey," her mom said. "But you have to be very careful. The bees don't like it when we take their honey. They might sting you if you get too close."

Anna nodded. She followed her mom to the big box. Her mom wore a funny hat with a net and gloves. She gave Anna a smaller hat and gloves to wear too. She opened the box and took out a frame. The frame was covered with wax and honey. Anna saw the bees crawling on it.

"Wow, mom, look at all the honey!" Anna said.

"Yes, honey, it's amazing. The bees work very hard to make it. They collect nectar from the flowers and turn it into honey. They store it in the wax cells for later. We can take some of it, but we have to leave some for them too. That's why we say thank you to the bees."

"Thank you, bees," Anna said. She smiled and waved at the bees. She hoped they heard her. She wanted to be nice to them. She knew they were nice to her. They gave her honey, and honey made her happy.

Tom and Lily were playing in the garden. They had a big box and some sticks. They wanted to make a raft. They worked hard and used tape and string to join the sticks to the box. They were very proud of their raft. It looked impressive.

"Let's go to the pond and sail our raft!" Tom said.

"OK, but we have to be careful. The pond is deep and there are fish and frogs," Lily said.

They carried their raft to the pond and put it on the water. They used a long stick to push the raft. It moved slowly and smoothly. They were having fun.

But then, something strange happened. The raft began to shrink. It became smaller and smaller. Tom and Lily were scared. They did not know why the raft was shrinking.

"Help! Our raft is shrinking!" Tom shouted.

"Maybe it is magic. Maybe a fairy or a wizard did it," Lily said.

They tried to grab the raft, but it was too small. It disappeared in the water. Tom and Lily were sad. They lost their raft.

They ran back to the house and told their mom what happened. She hugged them and said, "Don't worry, my loves. It was not magic. It was science. The box and the tape were made of paper and plastic. They got wet and dissolved in the water. That's why the raft shrank. Next time, use something that does not get wet, like wood or metal."

Tom and Lily learned something new. They felt better. They decided to make another raft, but this time, they used wood and metal. They hoped their new raft would not shrink.

"Thank you for coming to my party, Lily. You are my best friend," Anna said.

"Happy birthday, Anna. I have a present for you," Lily said. She gave Anna the envelope.

Anna opened it and saw the card. She gasped and clapped her hands.

"Wow, Lily, this is the most beautiful card ever. You are so creative. Thank you so much," Anna said.

Lily felt proud and happy. She and Anna went inside the house. They played games, sang songs and ate cake. The cake was yummy. It had chocolate and sprinkles.

But then, something bad happened. Billy, a boy from their class, came to the party. He was not invited. He was mean and rude. He grabbed Lily's card from Anna's hand and tore it in half. He laughed and said, "This card is ugly and silly. You are both babies."

Lily and Anna felt sad and angry. They cried and shouted at Billy.

"Go away, Billy. You are not welcome here. You are a bully and a liar. You ruined my card and my party," Anna said.

"Yeah, go away, Billy. You are not nice. You hurt our feelings. You have no friends," Lily said.

Billy felt scared and ashamed. He dropped the pieces of the card and ran away. He wished he had not been so mean.

Lily and Anna hugged each other and picked up the pieces of the card. They taped them together and put them on the wall. They decided to ignore Billy and have fun. They joined the other kids and had more cake and ice cream. They were happy again. They were best friends.

Then, he saw a boy who had no toys. The boy looked sad and lonely. He came near Tommy and asked, "Can I play with your car, please?" Tommy did not want to share his car. He said, "No, go away! This is my car. You are a stranger. I don't know you."

The boy smiled and said, "Sure, you can play with us. Thank you for sharing your car. You are not a stranger. You are a friend."

"Hello, teddy bear," Lily said. "We have a special mail for you. It is jam. Jam is good for you. It will make you feel better."

"Thank you, Lily and Ben," the teddy bear said in a low voice. "You are very kind. Can you open the jar for me? I am too weak to do it."

Lily and Ben nodded and tried to open the jar. But the lid was too tight and they could not twist it. They pulled and pushed and banged the jar, but it did not budge.

"Let me try," Ben said. "I am stronger than you."

"No, let me try," Lily said. "I am smarter than you."

They started to argue and tug at the jar. They did not notice that the jar was slipping from their hands. Suddenly, the jar fell to the floor and broke. The jam spilled everywhere, making a sticky mess.

"Oh no!" Lily and Ben cried. "We broke the jar! We wasted the jam! We made a mess! What will Mommy say?"

They looked at each other and felt sorry. They realized that they had been silly and selfish. They should have worked together and asked for help. They hugged and said sorry to each other and to the teddy bear.

"Sorry, teddy bear," Lily said. "We wanted to make you happy, but we made a mistake."

"Sorry, teddy bear," Ben said. "We wanted to help you, but we made a problem."

The teddy bear smiled and said, "It's okay, Lily and Ben. I appreciate your mail. But you know what? Jam is not the best medicine for me. Your love and friendship are. You are the best mail workers ever."

Lily and Ben smiled and hugged the teddy bear. Then they went to the kitchen and got a cloth and a mop. They cleaned up the jam and the glass. They learned that mail is a nice way to show you care, but you have to be careful and cooperative. And they learned that jam is better on bread than on the floor.

He ran back to his family and told them what happened. They hugged him and said he was brave. They gave him some cheese and water. Timmy was happy and safe. He learned a lesson. He decided not to drink milk from the table again. He drank water from the sink instead. It was not as delicious, but it was safer.

Tom is a big boy who likes to play with his cars and trucks. He has a lot of fun making them zoom and crash on the floor. But today, he is not feeling well. He has a sore throat and a fever. His mom says he has to take a pill to make him better.

Tom does not like pills. They are hard and bitter and make him gag. He does not want to swallow them. He says, "No, no, no! I don't want a pill!"

His mom says, "Tom, you have to take your pill. It will help you get rid of the germs that make you sick. It's not that big. Look, I'll show you."

She takes a small scale and puts the pill on one side. Then she takes a feather and puts it on the other side. The scale does not move. The pill and the feather weigh the same.

"See, Tom? The pill is as light as a feather. It won't hurt you. It will just slide down your throat. Come on, be a brave boy and open your mouth."

Tom looks at the scale and the pill and the feather. He thinks his mom is silly. How can a pill and a feather weigh the same? They are not the same at all. He does not believe her. He shakes his head and says, "No, no, no! I don't want a pill!"

His mom sighs and says, "Tom, please. You have to take your pill. How about this? If you take your pill, I'll let you play with the scale and the feather. You can weigh anything you want. Wouldn't that be fun?"

Tom thinks about it. He likes to play with new things. He likes to see what weighs more and what weighs less. He likes to make the scale go up and down. He decides to try the pill. He opens his mouth and his mom puts the pill in. He drinks some water and swallows the pill. It is not so bad. He feels proud of himself.

Tom hugs and kisses his mom. He feels happy. He says, "Thank you, mom. I love you. Can I play with the scale and the feather now?"

His mom says, "Yes, you can. But remember, don't weigh anything too heavy or too fragile. And don't put anything in your mouth that is not food. OK?"

Tom says, "OK, mom. I will be careful. I want to weigh my cars and trucks. And maybe my teddy bear. And maybe you. You are the best mom in the world."

His mom laughs and says, "You are the best son in the world. Now go and have fun. And I hope you feel better soon."

Tom runs to his room with the scale and the feather. He starts to weigh his toys and his mom. He has a lot of fun. He forgets about his sore throat and his fever. He thinks pills are not so bad after all. He thinks his mom is silly, but he loves her. He thinks he is a big boy who can do anything. He thinks he is happy.

She was always running away from Tommy and hiding under the bed, or in the closet, or behind the sofa. Tommy did not know why Fluffy was so scared of him. He wanted to be her friend.

One day, Tommy decided to follow Fluffy when she ran away. He saw her go into the kitchen and jump on the counter. There was a big cake on the counter. It was Tommy's birthday cake. His mom had made it for him and told him not to touch it until the party. Fluffy did not listen to mom. She licked the cake with her tongue and made a big mess.

"Fluffy, no!" Tommy shouted. He ran into the kitchen and tried to grab Fluffy. But Fluffy was faster. She jumped off the counter and ran out of the kitchen. Tommy chased her, but he slipped on the cake and fell on the floor. He hurt his knee and started to cry.

Mom heard the noise and came into the kitchen. She saw the cake, the kitten, and the boy. She was very angry. She picked up Fluffy and put her in a cage. She said, "Fluffy, you are a bad kitten. You ruined Tommy's cake. You have to stay in the cage until you learn to behave." She said to Tommy, "Tommy, I'm sorry about your cake. And your knee. Are you okay?"

Tommy nodded, but he felt sad. He did not want Fluffy to be in the cage. He did not want Fluffy to be a bad kitten. He wanted Fluffy to be a good kitten. He wanted Fluffy to love him. He said to mom, "Mom, can I talk to Fluffy? Maybe I can make her happy."

Mom sighed, but she said, "Okay, Tommy. You can talk to Fluffy. But be careful. She might scratch you or bite you. She is a troubled kitten. She needs a lot of patience and love."

Tommy went to the cage and looked at Fluffy. Fluffy looked at Tommy and meowed softly. Tommy said, "Fluffy, I'm sorry I yelled at you. I know you were hungry. But you can't eat my cake. That's not nice. You have to share. And you can't run away from me. That's not fun. You have to play with me. I love you, Fluffy. Do you love me?"

Fluffy looked at Tommy and meowed louder. She rubbed her head against the bars of the cage. She licked Tommy's finger. She purred. Tommy smiled. He said, "Fluffy, I think you love me too. You are a good kitten. Can you come out of the cage and be my friend?"

Mom saw Tommy and Fluffy and smiled too. She said, "Tommy, you are a good boy. You are very kind and gentle. I think Fluffy likes you too. She is a good kitten. She just needs some time and trust. Tommy nodded. He said, "Yes, mom. I want to help you. And I want to help Fluffy. Can she help us too?"

Mom laughed. She said, "Sure, Tommy. Fluffy can help us too. But only if she promises not to eat the cake again."

Tommy opened the cage and took out Fluffy. He hugged her and said, "Fluffy, do you promise not to eat the cake again?"

Fluffy meowed and nodded. She hugged Tommy back and said, "Yes, Tommy. I promise not to eat the cake again. I only want to eat your love."

Tommy, Fluffy, and mom went to the kitchen and cleaned up the cake. Then they made a new one. It was a beautiful cake. It had candles and sprinkles and a picture of Tommy and Fluffy on it. Tommy was very happy. He said, "Thank you, mom. Thank you, Fluffy. You are the best mom and the best kitten in the world. I love you both very much."

They hugged and kissed and sang and ate the cake. It was the best birthday ever.

Kim nodded. She also wanted to eat the cookie. She loved cookies. "Let's go outside and start the contest!" she said.

He drives the big truck fast and hard. He hits the books and blocks and pillows. He knocks them down. He makes a big mess. He laughs and says, "Look at me. I am the toughest driver. I make a big wreck."

But then, he does not see a hill. He drives the big truck over the hill. He loses control. The big truck flies in the air. It lands on the floor. It breaks into pieces. Tim is shocked. He says, "Oh no, oh no. What have I done? I broke the big truck. I broke Sam's big truck. He will be so mad at me."

He looks up and sees Sam. Sam is standing over him. He is angry and sad. He says, "Tim, you are a bad brother. You took my big truck. You broke it. You ruined our road. You are not tough. You are mean."

He picks up the pieces of his big truck. He says, "This was my favorite truck. You broke it. You are not my friend. Go away."

He walks away. He does not talk to Tim. He does not play with him. He is mad at him.

Tim feels sorry. He says, "Sam, I am sorry. I was wrong. I should not have taken your big truck. I should not have broken it. I should not have made a big wreck. I am sorry. Please, Sam, please. Can we be friends again?"

But Sam does not answer. He does not look at Tim. He does not forgive him.

Tim cries. He says, "I am sorry, Sam. I am sorry."

"Look, Tom, there are red fruits and yellow fruits and green fruits. They look yummy. Can we have some?" Lily asked.

"I don't know, Lily. Maybe they belong to someone. Maybe they are not good for us. We should ask Mom first," Tom said.

But Lily was too hungry and curious. She climbed the tree and reached for a red fruit. She pulled it hard and it came off. She took a bite and smiled. "Mmm, this is sweet and juicy. Try it, Tom, it's good," she said.

Tom climbed the tree too and picked a yellow fruit. He bit into it and made a face. "Yuck, this is sour and bitter. I don't like it," he said.

Suddenly, they heard a loud voice. "Hey, you kids, get off my tree! Those are my fruits, not yours. How dare you steal them? I'll teach you a lesson. Wait till I get my whip!" It was the farmer who owned the tree. He was angry and scary.

Lily and Tom were afraid. They dropped the fruits and jumped off the tree. They ran as fast as they could. They prayed that the farmer would not catch them. They ran all the way home and told Mom what happened.

Mom was not happy. She scolded them for being naughty and greedy. She said they should not take things that are not theirs. She said they should say sorry to the farmer and give him some of their toys. She said they should be more careful and listen to Tom next time.

Lily and Tom felt sorry and ashamed. They nodded and hugged Mom. They learned their lesson. They hoped the farmer would forgive them. They hoped he would not use his whip. They hoped they would never see him again.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play in the attic. They found many old things there, like hats, books, and toys. One day, they saw a big trunk in the corner. It was locked with a key.

"Let's open it!" Lily said. "Maybe there is something fun inside."

"But we don't have the key," Ben said. "How can we open it?"

Lily had an idea. She saw a hammer on the floor. She picked it up and swung it at the lock. "This will work," she said.

But she was clumsy. She missed the lock and hit the trunk instead. The trunk made a loud noise and shook. Lily and Ben heard a growl from inside.

"What was that?" Ben asked, scared.

"Maybe it's a monster," Lily said, also scared.

They ran to the door, but it was stuck. They tried to push it, but it did not move. They heard the trunk open behind them. They turned around and saw a big, furry creature with horns, claws, and teeth. It looked angry.

"Who are you?" it asked in a deep voice. "Why did you hit my trunk?"

Lily and Ben were very afraid. They did not know what to say. They wished they had not opened the trunk.

"Please don't hurt us," Lily said. "We are sorry. We did not know you were in there."

The creature looked at them. It saw that they were small and harmless. It felt sorry for them.

"I'm not going to hurt you," it said. "I'm just lonely. I've been in this trunk for a long time. No one ever comes to visit me."

"Who are you?" Ben asked.

"I'm a gruffalo," it said. "Do you know what a gruffalo is?"

Lily and Ben shook their heads. They had never heard of a gruffalo.

"A gruffalo is a magical animal," it said. "But people don't believe in us anymore. They think we are scary and bad. That's why I hide in this trunk. But I wish I had some friends."

Lily and Ben felt sorry for the gruffalo. They thought he was not scary and bad. He was just different and sad.

"Maybe we can be your friends," Lily said. "We like to play and have fun. We can show you our toys and books. We can tell you stories and jokes. We can make you happy."

The gruffalo smiled. He liked the sound of that. He wanted to play and have fun. He wanted to see their toys and books. He wanted to hear their stories and jokes. He wanted to be happy.

"Really?" he asked. "You would do that for me?"

"Sure," Ben said. "We don't mind that you are a gruffalo. We think you are cool and nice. We believe in you."

The gruffalo was very happy. He hugged Lily and Ben. They hugged him back. They opened the door and went downstairs. They played and laughed together. They became good friends. They learned that it did not matter what you look like or where you come from. What mattered was what was in your heart.

Lily and Tom were scared and sad. The pepper was gone. They had no toy. They had no friend. They went home. They did not play in the park again.

"Look, we printed stars!" Tom says. He is happy. He shows the paper to Mia.

"Wow, they are beautiful!" Mia says. She is happy too. She likes the stars. She sees many colors on the paper. She sees red, blue, yellow and green.

"Let's print more stars!" Tom says. He wants to make the paper full of stars.

"OK, let's print more stars!" Mia says. She agrees with Tom. She likes to print with Tom.

They print more stars on the paper. They have fun. They make a starry paper. They are proud of their work. They are healthy and happy. They are good friends.

Lily liked to dream. She dreamed of big things and small things, of flying and swimming, of animals and people. Sometimes she dreamed of going to the station with her dad. She wanted to see the trains and the buses and the people.

One day, her dad said, "Lily, do you want to go to the station with me? We can take the bus and see the trains."

Lily was very happy. She said, "Yes, yes, yes! I want to go to the station with you, dad!"

They got ready and went to the bus stop. They waited for the bus. Lily saw a big red bus coming. She said, "Look, dad, a big red bus!"

They got on the bus and paid the driver. They found a seat and looked out the window. Lily saw many things. She saw cars and bikes and shops and trees. She said, "Wow, dad, so many things!"

They got off the bus at the station. They walked to the platform. They saw a big yellow train. They heard a loud whistle. They saw the doors open and close. They saw people get on and off. Lily said, "Wow, dad, a big yellow train!"

They went to the other side of the platform. They saw a big blue train. They heard a loud horn. They saw the doors open and close. They saw people get on and off. Lily said, "Wow, dad, a big blue train!"

They watched the trains for a while. They saw different colors and shapes and sizes. They heard different sounds and voices. Lily said, "Dad, I like the station. It is fun and exciting."

Her dad smiled and hugged her. He said, "I'm glad you like the station, Lily. It is fun and exciting. But you know what? It is also normal. Many people go to the station every day. They go to work or school or visit their friends. They use the trains and buses to get around. The station is part of their life."

Lily nodded. She said, "I understand, dad. The station is normal for them. But it is still special for me. Because I get to go with you. And because I dreamed of it."

Her dad kissed her. He said, "You are very sweet, Lily. And you have a wonderful imagination. You can dream of anything you want. And maybe, one day, you can make your dreams come true."

Lily wanted a dog. She asked her mom and dad many times, but they said no. They said dogs are too much work and too loud. Lily was sad. She loved dogs. She liked to pet them and play with them.

One day, Lily saw a sign that said "Buy a dog for five coins". She had five coins in her piggy bank. She took them and ran to the sign. There was a man with a big box. He said, "Do you want a dog, little girl?"

Lily nodded. She gave him the coins. He opened the box and gave her a small, brown dog. It was hidden under a blanket. Lily was happy. She hugged the dog and named it Spot.

She ran back home with Spot. She wanted to show him to her mom and dad. But when she got home, they were angry. They saw the dog and said, "Where did you get that dog, Lily? You know you can't have a dog!"

Lily said, "But I bought him with my own coins. He is my dog. I love him. Please let me keep him."

Her mom and dad shook their heads. They said, "You can't buy a dog without asking us. You don't know how to take care of a dog. He might be sick or dirty or mean. You have to take him back to the man and get your coins back."

Lily cried. She didn't want to give up Spot. He was her friend. He licked her face and wagged his tail. She said, "No, no, no. He is not sick or dirty or mean. He is good and cute and nice. I want to keep him. Please, please, please."

Her mom and dad sighed. They saw how much Lily loved Spot. They felt sorry for her. They said, "OK, Lily. You can keep Spot. But you have to promise to take good care of him. You have to feed him and walk him and clean him. And you have to be quiet when he barks. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded. She said, "I promise, I promise, I promise. Thank you, thank you, thank you." She hugged her mom and dad and Spot. She was happy. She had a dog.

Sara was very hungry. She wanted to eat some bread and jam. She went to the kitchen and looked for the bread. But she could not find it. She saw a big jar of jam on the table. She opened it and put her hand inside. She took out some jam and put it in her mouth. It was very sweet and sticky. She liked it.

She wanted more jam. She looked for a spoon, but she could not find one. She saw a comb on the table. It was her mom's comb. She thought it looked like a spoon. She took the comb and dipped it in the jam. She put the comb in her mouth. It was very hard and pointy. It hurt her tongue. She did not like it.

She spit out the comb and the jam. She felt something wet on her face. It was blood. She was scared. She started to cry. She ran to her mom and showed her the comb and the blood. Her mom was shocked. She hugged Sara and took her to the bathroom. She cleaned her tongue and put a band-aid on it. She told Sara not to eat jam with a comb. She told her to use a spoon. She gave her some bread and jam and a glass of milk. Sara felt better. She said sorry to her mom and thanked her. She learned a lesson. She never ate jam with a comb again.

Tim and Sam were two dogs who liked to play together. They had a big yard with many toys and a cozy house. One day, they found a big bone in the yard. It was white and hard and smelled good.

"Wow, look at this bone!" Tim said. "It is so big and tasty. I want to eat it all by myself."

"No, you have to share it with me!" Sam said. "We are friends, and friends share things. It is not fair if you keep it all."

Tim and Sam started to growl and bark at each other. They both wanted the bone and did not want to share. They pulled and tugged on the bone, trying to take it away from each other.

Suddenly, they heard a loud roar. They looked up and saw a big bear coming towards them. The bear was hungry and angry. He saw the bone and wanted it too. He ran towards Tim and Sam, showing his sharp teeth and claws.

Tim and Sam were very scared. They dropped the bone and ran away. They hid behind the house and trembled. They wished they had not fought over the bone. They wished they had been more friendly and kind to each other.

The bear reached the bone and picked it up. He sniffed it and licked it. He was happy to find such a nice snack. He did not care about Tim and Sam. He ate the bone and left.

Tim and Sam peeked out from behind the house. They saw that the bone was gone. They felt sad and sorry. They realized that they had been foolish and greedy. They had lost their bone and almost lost their lives.

They looked at each other and said, "We are sorry. We should have shared the bone. We should have been better friends. Can we still be friends?"

They hugged and wagged their tails. They decided to forget about the bone and play together. They learned that friendship is more important than things. They were happy and safe again.

Sara was sad. Her toy horn was broken. She liked to play with it and make loud noises. But now it did not work. She tried to fix it with tape, but it was no good.

She went to her brother Tom. He was playing with his cars. She asked him, "Can you give me a horn? I want to play with it."

Tom looked at her. He saw her broken horn. He felt sorry for her. He said, "I have a horn. It is in my box. You can have it. But you have to be careful. It is not a toy. It is real."

He went to his box and took out a horn. It was big and shiny. It had a button on it. He gave it to Sara. She was happy. She said, "Thank you, Tom. You are nice. How do I use it?"

Tom said, "You press the button. But not too hard. And not too often. It is very loud. It can scare people and animals. It is for emergencies only."

Sara nodded. She pressed the button. The horn made a loud sound. It sounded like a train. Sara smiled. She liked the sound. She pressed the button again. And again. And again.

Tom said, "Stop, Sara. Stop. That is enough. You are making too much noise. You are bothering everyone. You have to stop."

But Sara did not stop. She pressed the button more and more. She did not listen to Tom. She did not see the angry faces of their mom and dad. She did not hear the barking of the dog. She did not notice the birds flying away.

She only heard the horn. And she liked it. She thought it was fun. She did not know she was doing something wrong. She was only three years old.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. Sometimes they missed the ball and it rolled away. Then they had to chase it before it went too far.

One time, the ball went over the fence and into the street. Tom and Lily ran to the fence and looked for the ball. They saw it near a big building with a cross on top. Lily said, "That is a church. My mom and dad go there on Sunday. They say it is God's house."

Tom said, "Can we get our ball from the church? Maybe God will let us play with it."

Lily said, "I don't know. Maybe we should ask someone. But we have to be careful. The street is busy and cars are fast. They can hurt us if we are not careful."

Tom and Lily looked around and saw a man walking on the sidewalk. He was wearing a black suit and a white collar. He looked kind and friendly. Lily said, "Maybe he works at the church. Maybe he can help us."

Tom and Lily waved at the man and called, "Hello, sir. Can you help us? Our ball went into the church. Can we get it back?"

The man smiled and said, "Hello, children. I am the pastor of the church. I can help you get your ball back. But first, you have to guess something. What do you think is inside the church?"

Tom and Lily thought hard. They tried to guess what was inside the church. Tom said, "Is it a big book?"

Lily said, "Is it a big candle?"

The pastor said, "Those are good guesses, but they are not right. There is something more important inside the church. It is something that you cannot see, but you can feel. It is something that God gives us and we give to each other. It is something that makes us happy and strong. Do you know what it is?"

Tom and Lily looked at each other and said, "Is it love?"

The pastor said, "Yes, it is love. You are very smart, children. Love is inside the church, and outside the church, and everywhere. God loves you, and I love you, and you love each other. And love is more precious than any ball. But I know you want your ball back, so come with me. I will show you where it is. And then you can play with it, but be careful not to kick it over the fence again."

Tom and Lily said, "Thank you, pastor. You are very nice. We will be careful. And we love you too." They followed the pastor to the church and got their ball back. Then they went back to the park and played with their ball. They were happy and grateful. They learned something new about the church and about love.

Anna liked to help her mom in the garden. She watered the flowers, pulled the weeds, and smelled the herbs. Her mom taught her the names of the herbs, like mint, rosemary, and basil. Anna liked mint the best, because it was fresh and sweet.

One day, Anna saw a little bird in the garden. It was brown and white, with a red spot on its head. It was hopping on the ground, looking for seeds. Anna wanted to play with the bird, so she ran towards it. But the bird was scared, and flew away.

"Anna, stop!" her mom said. "You have to be gentle with the birds. They are not toys. They are living things, like you and me. They need space and respect."

"But I just wanted to say hello," Anna said. "I like the bird. It is pretty and sings nice songs."

"I know, sweetie," her mom said. "But the bird doesn't know that. It thinks you are a big, scary thing that wants to hurt it. If you want to be friends with the bird, you have to be quiet and calm. Maybe you can offer it some seeds or some herbs. Maybe it will come closer and trust you."

Anna nodded. She understood. She picked some mint leaves from the garden, and put them on her palm. She walked slowly and softly to the spot where she saw the bird. She sat down on the grass, and held out her hand. She shut her mouth, and waited.

After a while, the bird came back. It saw the mint leaves, and smelled them. It liked the smell. It flew to a nearby branch, and looked at Anna. It saw that she was not moving or making noise. It felt curious and safe. It flew to Anna's hand, and pecked at the mint. Anna smiled, and stayed still. She felt the bird's feathers and beak. She heard its heartbeat. She was happy.

The bird ate the mint, and sang a thank you song. It flew away, but came back the next day. And the next. And the next. Anna and the bird became friends. Anna learned to be gentle with the birds, and the birds learned to trust Anna. Her mom was proud of her.

Lily was a little girl who loved flowers. She liked to pick them and smell them and make crowns for her dolls. One day, she saw a big field of daisies. They were white and yellow and very pretty. She wanted to pick some for her mommy.

She ran to the field and started to pick the daisies. She saw one that was very big and bright. She wanted to reach it, but it was too far. She stretched her arm and stood on her toes, but she could not touch it. She felt anxious. She wanted that daisy very much.

She looked around and saw a big rock. She had an idea. She climbed on the rock and tried to reach the daisy again. She was closer, but still not enough. She leaned forward and reached with her fingers. She almost had it, but then she lost her balance. She fell off the rock and landed on the grass.

She cried out loud. She hurt her knee and her elbow. She was sad and scared. She wanted her mommy. She looked at the daisy. It was still there, but she did not want it anymore. She wanted a hug.

She heard a voice. It was her mommy. She had heard her cry and came to see what was wrong. She saw Lily on the grass and ran to her. She picked her up and hugged her. She kissed her knee and her elbow and wiped her tears. She said, "It's okay, Lily. I'm here. You are brave and strong. I love you."

Just then, he heard a voice. It said, "There, there, little bear. Don't cry. I believe I can help you!" He looked up and saw a kind-looking dragonfly hovering nearby. With a wave of its wings, it let him know to come closer.

The bear slowly approached, feeling a bit scared. The dragonfly asked, "Would you like me to try to help you get your knob loose?" The bear nodded, hoping that the dragonfly could help. 

The dragonfly then told the bear to step back a bit, and it began to spin its wings rapidly. Soon a gentle breeze surrounded the bear, and the air started to urge against the knob. Eventually, the knob became loose! The bear was so relieved and excited, he cheered with joy.

The dragonfly had saved the day, and the bear thanked it with a big hug. From then on, they were the best of friends.

Lily was very scared, but she remembered what her mom had told her about witches. She knew that witches don't like nice things, so she gave the witch a pretty flower. The witch was so happy that she let Lily go home safely. From that day on, the witch was never mean again and always decorated her house with pretty things.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sun. One day, she saw a shiny penny on the ground. It was made of copper and it sparkled in the sun. 

Lily picked up the penny and showed it to her friend, Max. Max was a polite boy who always said please and thank you. He said, "That's a nice penny, Lily. Where did you find it?" 

Lily smiled and said, "I found it over there by the tree. Do you want to dare me to flip it and see if it lands on heads or tails?" 

Max thought for a moment and then said, "Sure, I dare you to flip it." 

Lily tossed the penny in the air and it landed on heads. She smiled and said, "I won! I won!" 

Later that day, Lily and Max went to the store to buy some candy. Lily remembered her lucky penny and put it in her pocket. When they got to the store, Lily saw a shiny red lollipop. She wanted it so badly, but she didn't have enough money. 

Max saw how sad Lily was and said, "Don't worry, I'll buy it for you." 

Lily was so happy and thanked Max for being so polite and kind. She knew that her lucky penny had brought her good luck and a good friend.

They poked the hole harder and faster, hoping to make something come out. Suddenly, they heard a loud hiss and saw a flash of green. A snake came out of the hole and coiled around the stick.

"Help! Help!" Anna and Ben screamed. They dropped the stick and ran back to their cabin.

Their mom heard their screams and came out to see what was wrong. She saw the snake on the stick and picked it up carefully.

"Don't worry, kids. This is not a bad snake. It is a garter snake. It is harmless and intelligent. It was probably just scared by your poking," she said.

She took the snake to the woods and let it go. She told Anna and Ben to be more careful and respectful of the animals in the woods.

Anna and Ben felt sorry for the snake and learned their lesson. They decided to poke only things that were not alive, like rocks and leaves. They still liked to explore the woods, but they did not bother the animals anymore.

But then, a big truck came down the road. It was very loud and fast. It did not see the toys on the road. It ran over them and broke them. The toys were smashed and dirty. Tom and Lily were very sad and angry. They cried and shouted at the truck.

"Go away, truck! You spoil our game! You spoil our toys! You are mean and bad!"

The truck driver heard them and stopped. He got out of the truck and saw the toys. He felt sorry for Tom and Lily. He said he was sorry and he did not mean to spoil their game. He said he would buy them new toys. He said he would be more careful next time.

Tom and Lily stopped crying and shouting. They saw that the truck driver was nice and sorry. They said they forgave him and thanked him. They said they would play somewhere else next time. They said they would be more careful too.

The truck driver smiled and gave them a hug. He said he was glad they were not hurt. He said he hoped they would have a perfect day. He got back in his truck and drove away.

Tom and Lily picked up their toys and went back to their house. They put their toys in their box and said goodbye to them. They said they would remember their game and their trip to the zoo. They said they would have new toys soon. They said they still loved each other. They hugged and smiled. They had a perfect day.

Mia and Ben were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. Sometimes they missed the ball and it rolled away. They had to chase it before it went too far.

One day, the sky was dark and cloudy. Mia and Ben heard a loud noise. It was thunder. They looked up and saw flashes of light. It was lightning. They were scared and ran to their mom.

"Mom, mom, can we go home?" they asked. "It is going to rain."

Mom nodded and picked up their ball. She held their hands and walked to the car. On the way, they felt drops of water on their faces. It was raining.

They got in the car and buckled their seat belts. Mom started the car and drove away. The rain was heavy and noisy. They could not see much outside the window.

"Look, look!" Mia shouted suddenly. She pointed to the sky. "A rainbow!"

Ben looked and saw it too. It was a big arc of colors. It was bright and beautiful. It made them happy.

"How did the rainbow get there?" Ben asked.

Mom smiled and explained. "When the sun shines on the rain drops, they make the colors. The colors are always there, but we can only see them when the sun and the rain are together."

Mia and Ben nodded. They liked the colors. They tried to name them. Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple.

They reached their home and got out of the car. They ran to the door and opened it. They saw their cat, Fluffy, waiting for them. He was wet and muddy. He had been outside in the rain.

"Fluffy, you are naughty!" Mia scolded. "You should stay inside when it rains. You are dirty and cold."

Fluffy meowed and rubbed against their legs. He wanted to cuddle and play. Mia and Ben laughed and hugged him. They loved their cat, even when he was naughty.

They went inside and changed their clothes. Mom gave them some cookies and milk. They ate and drank and told mom about the rainbow. They drew pictures of it with their crayons. They had a good day, even though it rained.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big bird on a tree. The bird has many colors. It has a red head, a blue body, and a yellow tail. Lily and Tom think the bird is pretty.

"Hello, bird!" Lily says. "Do you want to be our friend?"

The bird looks at them and makes a loud noise. "Squawk! Squawk!"

Tom has a bag of bread. He breaks a piece and throws it to the bird. "Here, bird. Have some food. Maybe you are hungry."

The bird flies down and catches the bread. It eats it and makes another noise. "Mmm! Mmm!"

Lily and Tom are happy. They think the bird likes them. They throw more bread to the bird. The bird eats more and more.

But then, the bird stops eating. It makes a funny face. It spits out the bread. It shakes its head. It looks angry.

"Yuck! Yuck!" the bird says. "This bread is sour. It is bad. It hurts my mouth."

Lily and Tom are surprised. They did not know the bread was sour. They look at the bag. They see a green strip on the bread. The bread is moldy. They feel sorry for the bird.

"We are sorry, bird. We did not know the bread was sour. We wanted to feed you. We wanted to be nice." Lily says.

The bird looks at them and calms down. It sees that they are sorry. It sees that they are nice. It flies back to the tree. It makes a soft noise.

"It is okay. It is okay." the bird says. "You are nice. You are my friends. Thank you for trying to feed me. Next time, bring me fresh bread. Or better, bring me seeds. I like seeds. Seeds are good."

Lily and Tom smile. They are glad the bird is not angry. They are glad the bird is their friend. They say goodbye to the bird. They promise to bring seeds next time. They go home and tell their mom about the bird. They hope to see the bird again.

Sam says: "I want that car. It looks cool."

Tom says: "Me too. But we have no money. How can we get it?"

Sam thinks. He says: "I have an idea. We can take the car from the store. No one will see us."

Tom feels scared. He says: "That is bad. That is stealing. We will get in trouble."

Sam says: "No, we won't. Trust me. It will be easy. Come on, let's go."

Sam and Tom walk to the store. They see the car on a shelf. It is shiny and new. Sam grabs the car and runs. Tom follows him. They run to the park.

But they do not see the old man. The old man works at the store. He sees them take the car. He is angry. He runs after them. He shouts: "Stop! You are thieves! Give me back the car!"

Sam and Tom hear the old man. They are afraid. They drop the car and run away. The old man picks up the car. He calls the police.

Sam and Tom hide behind a tree. They are sad. They are sorry. They wish they did not take the car. They wish they did not listen to Sam. They wish they did not see the billboard.

Lily and Mom walk to the grocery. Lily likes to walk with Mom. She sees many things on the way. She sees a big dog, a red car, a yellow flower. She says hello to them.

"Mom, can we get some candy at the grocery?" Lily asks.

"No, Lily, candy is not healthy. We need to get healthy food, like fruits and vegetables. They make us strong and happy," Mom says.

Lily makes a sad face. She loves candy. She thinks candy makes her happy too.

They get to the grocery. Mom puts some apples, bananas, carrots, and broccoli in the cart. Lily sees a big jar of candy on the shelf. It has many colors and shapes. It looks yummy. She wants to grab it.

"Mom, look, candy!" Lily says, pointing to the jar.

Mom turns around and sees the jar. She smiles. She has a surprise for Lily.

"Lily, do you remember the sticker book you wanted? The one with the animals and the stars?" Mom asks.

"Yes, Mom, I remember. I really want it," Lily says.

"Well, I have it here, in my bag. I got it for you, because you have been a good girl. But you can only have it if you promise me something," Mom says.

"What is it, Mom?" Lily asks.

"You have to promise me that you will eat some of the healthy food we got, and not ask for candy anymore. Can you do that?" Mom asks.

Lily thinks for a moment. She really wants the sticker book. But she also wants the candy. She looks at the jar, then at Mom, then at the cart. She makes a decision.

"OK, Mom, I promise. I will eat some healthy food, and no candy. Can I have the sticker book now?" Lily asks.

Mom hugs Lily and gives her the sticker book. Lily is very happy. She opens the book and sees the animals and the stars. She thanks Mom and gives her a kiss.

They pay for the food and walk back home. Lily holds the sticker book in her hand. She forgets about the candy. She thinks about where to put the stickers. She thinks she made a good choice. She thinks Mom is the best.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play together, but sometimes they fight. One day, they fight over a toy car. Lily wants to drive it, but Ben says it is his. They pull and push and shout.

"Mine!" Ben says.

"No, mine!" Lily says.

Mom hears them and comes to their room. She is not happy. She takes the toy car and puts it on a shelf.

"Stop fighting!" Mom says. "You are twins. You should unite and share. If you keep fighting, you will have no toys and no stories."

Lily and Ben feel sad. They do not want to lose their toys and stories. They look at each other and say sorry.

"Sorry, Lily," Ben says.

"Sorry, Ben," Lily says.

They hug and smile. Mom sees them and smiles too. She gives them back the toy car.

"Good twins," Mom says. "Now you can play together and have fun. But soon it will be evening, and you will have to get ready for bed."

Lily and Ben nod. They play with the toy car, taking turns to drive it. They have fun and laugh. They are happy to unite and share.

When it is evening, Mom comes to their room again. She helps them brush their teeth and put on their pajamas. She tucks them in their beds and gives them each a kiss.

"Good night, Lily," Mom says.

"Good night, Ben," Mom says.

"Good night, Mom," Lily and Ben say.

Mom turns off the light and leaves the room. Lily and Ben snuggle in their beds. They feel comfortable and warm. They are happy to be twins. They fall asleep and dream of toy cars.

Lily was a little girl who liked to sleep a lot. She did not like to wake up early and go to school. She always struggled to get out of bed and put on her clothes. Her mom and dad tried to help her, but she was grumpy and slow.

One day, Lily had a bad dream. She dreamed that she was late for school and everyone laughed at her. She woke up with a start and felt scared. She looked at the clock and saw that it was still dark outside. She thought it was time to go to school, but it was not. It was still night.

She ran to her mom and dad's room and knocked on the door. "Mom, dad, I had a bad dream. Can I sleep with you?" she asked. Her mom and dad opened the door and saw her. They hugged her and said, "Of course, sweetie. Come in, it's cool in here. You can sleep with us until the sun comes up."

Lily felt happy and safe. She snuggled with her mom and dad and closed her eyes. She thought that maybe waking up early was not so bad after all. She decided to try harder to be ready for school and not struggle so much. She realized that her mom and dad loved her and wanted her to learn and have fun. She smiled and fell asleep again.

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches that sleeping well and waking up early are important for having a good day and learning new things. It also shows that parents are supportive and caring, and that bad dreams are not real.

Foreshadowing or setup and payoff: The story uses foreshadowing by showing that Lily likes to sleep a lot and struggles to wake up, which leads to her having a bad dream. It also uses payoff by showing that her bad dream makes her appreciate waking up and being with her mom and dad.

"Let's taste it!" Ben said.

"Yuck, yuck, yuck!" they said.

They heard their mom coming into the kitchen. She saw the mess they made and the bowl of soup. She was angry.

"What did you do?" she asked.

"We made soup!" Anna and Ben said.

"That's not soup, that's garbage!" mom said. "You wasted food and made a mess. And you could have burned yourself with the hot water. You are in big trouble!"

She took the bowl and threw it in the trash. She turned off the faucet and cleaned the kitchen. She sent Anna and Ben to their room without dinner. They cried and said they were sorry. But mom did not listen. She was too mad.

You can show them you are friendly and curious. You can learn from them and teach them. You can share your language and learn theirs. Language is fun and amazing, but it is not the only way to connect with others."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She had a pretty scarf. Lucy loved her scarf very much. One day, it was very cold outside. Lucy wanted to go play with her friends. Her mommy said, "I recommend you wear your scarf."

Lucy put on her scarf and went outside. She saw her friends, Tom and Sue. They were playing in the snow. Tom and Sue were cold. Lucy said, "You should wear a scarf like me. It helps keep you warm."

The ant thought, "I should have waited for a better time to cross the river." The ant learned that it is important to be patient and wait for the right time to do something. This way, we can avoid bad things from happening.

Tiny saw Hoppy with the flag and said, "Wow, that is a pretty flag! Can I see it?" Hoppy nodded and showed Tiny the flag. Tiny liked the flag too and they both decided to share it. From that day on, Hoppy and Tiny played with the flag every day and became the best of friends.

The rabbit wanted to see what the trap was for. So, it hopped up to the trap and began to follow the strings. The strings led the rabbit deeper and deeper into the forest until it found a big, juicy carrot waiting in the centre. 

The rabbit started to eat the carrot, but then it saw something else. It was a beautiful butterfly flying around the carrot. The butterfly was very graceful, just like the rabbit.

The rabbit stopped and watched the butterfly for a while, and then followed it. As the rabbit followed the butterfly, it flew around different kinds of plants, but it never stopped to rest. The rabbit followed the butterfly until it could not go any further and came back home. 

The rabbit found a new appreciation for life and the beauty of nature because of that graceful butterfly.

Once upon a time, there was a very hard grape. The grape didn't like how hard it was, so it wanted to solve the problem. It started to look for a way to become softer. It asked around, but no one seemed to know what would work.

The next day, the grape saw a bee flying around. The bee stopped and asked the grape why it was so sad. The grape explained that it was too hard and wanted to become softer. The bee knew just what to do!

The bee explained that if the grape rolled around on the ground, the dirt and rocks would help the grape become softer. The grape was so excited and tried rolling around on the ground right away. Sure enough, the dirt and rocks made it softer! The grape was so happy!

From then on, the grape stayed soft and never got too hard again. The end.

The snake was hissing at her, but luckily, a friendly dog came to save her. He barked loudly and the snake quickly ran away. The little girl was so happy to be safe and gave the dog a big hug.

The little girl returned home feeling proud of her adventure and of the dog who saved her. She thanked him by giving him a scratch behind the ears, and wrapped the pink scarf around his neck. From that day forward, she decided to always keep her scarf close by, just in case she ever needed saving again.

He chased the cheese all around, until eventually, the cheese just stopped and stared at him. 

The mouse didn't know what to do. He realized that he would never be able to catch the cheese. So, he decided to surrender. He put his front paws up in the air and said, "I give up. Please, can I have some cheese?" 

The cheese just stared at the mouse for a bit, and then disappeared! But when the mouse looked around, he saw that the cheese had left a big plate of delicious cheese for him. He was so happy! The mouse thanked the cheese for his kindness and then enjoyed the yummy cheese. 

Moral of the story: When you surrender, good things can happen.

So, Tim thought of a better way to help the snake. He found a big stick and carefully used it to lift the snake out of the hole. The snake was happy and said, "Thank you, Tim! You are very kind."

From that day on, Tim and the green snake were good friends. They played together in the big green forest every day. Tim learned that being kind and helping others was the best way to make friends. And they all lived happily ever after.

She walks around the house. She sees her cat on the window. She takes a picture of her cat. She sees her doll on the bed. She takes a picture of her doll. She sees her brother in the kitchen. He is eating a cookie. She takes a picture of her brother.

She is happy. She has many pictures. She wants to show them to her mom. She runs to the table. She puts the camera back. She sees her mom coming in. She says, "Mom, look! I design pictures with your camera!"

Anna and Ben are playing with their toys on the rug. They have cars, dolls, blocks and books. They are having fun and making noises.

"Vroom, vroom, my car is fast!" Ben says.

"My doll is pretty, she has a dress and a hat!" Anna says.

They play for a long time, until their mom calls them for lunch.

"Anna, Ben, come and eat, it's time for lunch!" Mom says.

Anna and Ben run to the kitchen. They are hungry and want to eat. They forget their toys on the rug.

They eat soup, bread and cheese. They drink juice and water. They talk to mom and dad.

"Did you have fun playing?" Mom asks.

"Yes, we did, we have many toys!" Anna says.

"What did you play with?" Dad asks.

"We played with cars, dolls, blocks and books!" Ben says.

They finish their lunch and say thank you. They want to go back to play.

But when they go to the living room, they see a big mess. Their toys are not on the rug. They are all over the floor, the sofa, the table and the lamp. Some are broken, some are dirty, some are missing.

"What happened?" Anna cries.

"Who did this?" Ben shouts.

They look around and see a big dog. The dog is wagging its tail and panting. The dog has a car in its mouth and a doll in its paw.

"Bad dog, bad dog, give us our toys!" Anna and Ben say.

The dog drops the car and the doll and runs away. It goes to the door and barks.

Mom and dad come to see what is wrong. They see the dog and the mess.

"Oh no, this is Rex, our neighbor's dog. He must have sneaked in when we opened the door for lunch. He likes to play with toys, but he doesn't know how to be gentle. He is not a bad dog, just a silly dog." Mom says.

"I'm sorry, kids, your toys are ruined. We will talk to our neighbor and get you new toys. Don't be sad, it's not your fault. You just forgot to put them away." Dad says.

Anna and Ben are still sad, but they understand. They hug mom and dad and say it's okay.

They are clever kids, they learn from their mistake. They will not forget their toys on the rug again. They will put them in a box or a basket. They will also be careful with the door and the dog. They will still have fun playing, but they will also be tidy and safe.

One day, a boy named Tom and his dog Spot went to the park. They liked to play with the ball and run on the grass. But they saw an old man sitting on a bench. He had a bottle in his hand. He looked angry and sad.

"Hello, old man," Tom said. "Why are you sad?"

"Go away, boy," the old man said. "This is my poison. I want to drink it and die. I have no one who loves me."

Tom felt sorry for the old man. He wanted to help him. He said, "Don't drink the poison, old man. It will make you sick and hurt. You have me and Spot. We can be your friends. We love you."

The old man looked at Tom and Spot. He saw their happy faces and wagging tails. He felt something warm in his heart. He said, "Really? You love me? You want to be my friends?"

"Yes, old man," Tom said. "We do. Come and play with us. We can have fun together."

The old man smiled. He put down the bottle. He said, "OK, boy. OK, dog. You are very kind. You make me happy. Let's go and play."

Tom and Spot were happy too. They took the old man by the hand and ran to the ball. They threw it and caught it and laughed. The old man felt young again. He forgot about the poison. He only thought about his new friends. They played until the sun went down. Then they hugged and said goodbye. They promised to come back the next day. The old man went home with a smile. He was not sad anymore. He was not alone anymore. He had Tom and Spot. He had love.

Tom and Lily liked to play pretend. They had a big box that they made into a house. They painted it green, because green was their favorite color. They put some pillows and toys inside the box and pretended it was their cozy home.

One day, they invited their friend Sam to play with them. Sam came to their house and saw the green box. He did not like green. He said, "Your house is ugly. Green is a bad color. My house is red and much better." He kicked the box and made a hole in it.

Tom and Lily were very sad. They worked hard to make their house. They liked green. They did not want to play with Sam anymore. They told him to go away. Sam felt sorry. He realized he was mean and rude. He said, "I'm sorry, Tom and Lily. I was wrong. Your house is nice. Green is a good color. Can I play with you?"

Tom and Lily thought for a moment. They decided to forgive Sam. They said, "It's okay, Sam. We are still friends. You can play with us. But you have to help us fix our house." Sam agreed. He helped them tape the hole and paint the box again. They all played pretend happily in their green house.

The moral of the story is: Don't judge others by their preferences. Be kind and respectful. Apologize when you make a mistake. Forgive and help your friends.

"Let's go see the mist!" Ben said. He ran to the mist.

They reached the mist. It was cold and wet. They could not see very well. They heard a loud noise.

"What is that?" Sam asked.

"I don't know. Maybe a big car or a train," Ben said.

They were scared. They wanted to go back. But they did not know which way to go.

"Help! Help!" they shouted. But no one heard them.

They decided to crawl on the ground. They hoped to find the grass again. They crawled and crawled. But they only found more mist.

They got dirty and tired. They cried and hugged each other.

They did not know that they were crawling on a road. They did not see the big truck that was coming fast. They did not hear the horn that was honking.

The truck hit them. They did not feel anything.

One day, a big bear was walking in the forest. He was hungry and wanted to find some honey. He saw a tree with a hole and smelled something sweet. He thought there was honey inside the hole.

He climbed the tree and put his paw in the hole. But he felt something sticky and sharp. It was a bee's nest! The bees were angry and came out of the hole. They flew around the bear and stung him. The bear cried out, "Ow, ow, ow! Go away, bees! I just want some honey!"

A little bird was sitting on a branch nearby. He saw the bear and felt sorry for him. He flew to the bear and said, "Hello, bear. I can help you. I know where there is some honey. Follow me."

The bear was happy and said, "Thank you, bird. You are very kind. Where is the honey?"

The bird said, "It is in a jar by the river. Someone left it there. But you have to be careful. There is a lid on the jar. You have to attach it back after you take some honey. Or the bees will find it and take it all."

The bear nodded and said, "OK, bird. I will do that. Let's go."

The bird and the bear went to the river. They saw the jar with the honey. The bear opened the lid and took a big lick. He smiled and said, "Mmm, this is good honey. I like it."

The bird said, "I'm glad you like it, bear. But don't forget to attach the lid back. Or the bees will come."

The bear said, "Don't worry, bird. I will attach the lid back. I don't want the bees to sting me again."

The bear and the bird shared the honey. They were happy and became friends. They attached the lid back and left the jar by the river. They walked back to the forest, talking and laughing. The bees did not bother them anymore.

You have to put them from small to big. You have to write the numbers. You have to be quiet. You have to do your best. Are you ready?"

"But I want to poke him. He is soft and cold. I like to poke things," Max said.

He reached out his hand and poked the snowman's nose. The carrot fell off and rolled away. The snowman looked sad.

"Max, why did you do that? You made our snowman lose his nose. Now he is not smiling anymore," Lily said.

She picked up the carrot and tried to put it back. But the hole was too big and the carrot was too small. It did not fit.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I did not mean to make him sad. I just wanted to poke him. Can we fix him?" Max said.

He looked around and saw a bigger carrot on the ground. He ran and got it. He made a new hole in the snowman's face and pushed the carrot in. The snowman looked happy again.

"Look, Lily. I fixed him. He has a new nose. He is smiling again," Max said.

Lily smiled too. She hugged Max and said, "Thank you, Max. You are a good brother. I forgive you. Let's play with our snowman some more."

They put on their gloves and their hats. They wrapped their scarves around their necks. They were not cold anymore. They played with their snowman until it was time to go home. They said goodbye to their snowman and promised to come back tomorrow. They went inside and had some hot chocolate. They were very happy.

But the big fat duck does not listen. It eats all the bread. It does not share with the thin duck or the other ducks. The thin duck is sad and hungry. It swims away.

Lila and Tom feel sorry for the thin duck. They want to help it. They look for more bread. But they do not have any more. They have given all their bread to the pond.

"Oh, no, Tom, what can we do?" Lila asks.

"I don't know, Lila, maybe we can find some seeds or worms." Tom says.

They look around the pond. They do not see any seeds or worms. They only see rocks and dirt. They are sad and frustrated.

They hear a loud splash. They turn around. They see the thin duck. It is not in the pond. It is in the air. It is flying away.

"Bye, thin duck! We hope you find some food!" Lila and Tom shout.

But the thin duck does not hear them. It does not fly far. It is too weak and tired. It falls to the ground. It does not get up. It is dead.

Lila and Tom are shocked and sad. They run to the thin duck. They try to wake it up. But it is too late. The thin duck is gone.

They cry and hug each other. They wish they could have helped the thin duck. They wish the big fat duck was not so greedy. They wish the world was not so cruel.

The end.

Lily liked to wear her pink skirt. It had many stars on it that would shine when she moved. She felt like a princess in her skirt. She wanted to show it to her friend Mia, who lived next door.

She asked her mom if she could go to Mia's house. Her mom said yes, but she had to be careful. She had to look both ways before crossing the street. She had to hold her mom's hand. She had to stay away from the big dogs that barked loudly. Lily nodded and said she would be safe.

She and her mom walked to Mia's house. Lily saw Mia waiting for her on the porch. She ran to hug her. "Look at my skirt!" she said. "It has stars that shine!"

Mia gasped. "It's so pretty!" she said. "Can I try it on?"

Lily smiled. She liked to share with Mia. She took off her skirt and gave it to Mia. Mia put it on and twirled around. The stars shone brightly.

But then, a big dog came out of nowhere. It saw the shining stars and thought they were toys. It ran towards Mia and barked loudly. Mia screamed and dropped the skirt. The dog grabbed the skirt and ran away.

Lily and Mia were very scared. They cried and hugged each other. Lily's mom and Mia's mom came out and saw what happened. They comforted the girls and chased the dog away. They got the skirt back, but it was torn and dirty.

Lily was sad. She loved her skirt. She thought it was ruined. But Mia said, "Don't worry, Lily. We can fix it. We can sew it and wash it and make it shine again. It will still be your princess skirt."

Lily smiled. She was glad to have Mia as her friend. She said, "Thank you, Mia. You are very kind. You are my best friend."

They hugged again and went inside. They played with their dolls and had cookies and milk. They forgot about the dog and the skirt. They were happy and safe.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the forest with her dad. They wanted to pick some red fruits for mom. Lily liked the forest, but she was afraid of the big and loud animals that lived there.

"Dad, can we go home soon?" Lily asked. "I am tired and hungry."

"Not yet, Lily. We need more fruits. Look, there are some over there." Dad pointed to a bush. "You stay here and I will get them."

Lily nodded and sat on a rock. She saw a butterfly and tried to catch it. She ran after the butterfly and did not see where she was going. She went far away from the rock and the bush.

Suddenly, she heard a growl. She turned around and saw a big wolf. The wolf had sharp teeth and yellow eyes. It looked hungry and angry. Lily was very scared. She wanted to run back to dad, but the wolf was faster. She looked for a place to hide.

She saw a hole under a tree. She ran to the hole and crawled inside. The hole was dark and small, but it was better than the wolf. She hoped the wolf would not find her.

The wolf came to the tree and sniffed. It smelled Lily. It tried to dig the hole with its paws, but the hole was too deep. It tried to bite the tree, but the tree was too hard. It tried to push the tree, but the tree was too heavy. The wolf was angry and tired. It gave up and left.

Lily heard the wolf go away. She was happy and relieved. She waited for a while, then peeked out of the hole. She saw dad coming. He was looking for her and calling her name.

"Lily, where are you?" Dad shouted.

"Dad, I'm here!" Lily cried. She ran out of the hole and hugged dad.

"Lily, I was so worried. What happened?" Dad asked.

Lily told dad about the wolf and the hole. Dad was shocked and proud. He hugged Lily and said, "You are very brave, Lily. You did well to hide from the wolf. But next time, please stay close to me. The forest can be dangerous."

Lily nodded and said, "I'm sorry, dad. I won't run away again. Can we go home now?"

"Yes, Lily. Let's go home. We have enough fruits for mom. And maybe a cake for you." Dad smiled and took Lily's hand. They walked back to the car and left the forest. Lily was happy and safe. She learned a lesson and had a story to tell.

Tommy liked to read books. He had many books in his bookcase. He liked to look at the pictures and learn new things. Sometimes he read to his teddy bear, who was his best friend.

They were stuck together. Tommy tried to pull them apart, but he ripped them. He heard a loud tear. He felt sad and scared.

Mommy heard the tear too. She came into Tommy's room and saw the ripped book. She was angry. She said, "Tommy, what did you do? This was Daddy's book. He loved it very much. It was very old and special. You should not have touched it. You are a bad boy."

Tommy started to cry. He said, "I'm sorry, Mommy. I didn't know. I just wanted to read it. I like dragons. Please don't be mad at me. Please don't tell Daddy."

Mommy saw Tommy's tears and felt sorry for him. She said, "It's okay, Tommy. I know you didn't mean to hurt the book. You were curious and excited. But you have to be careful with other people's things. You have to ask before you take them. And you have to be gentle with them. Do you understand?"

Tommy nodded. He said, "I understand, Mommy. I will be careful next time. I will ask before I take. I will be gentle. I love you, Mommy."

Mommy hugged Tommy. She said, "I love you too, Tommy. I forgive you. But you have to say sorry to Daddy too. He will be sad when he sees his book. But he will forgive you too. He loves you very much."

Tommy smiled too. He said, "Okay, Mommy. Let's go and find a book. Maybe one with a dragon. But a nice dragon. Not a grumpy dragon."

Lily and Tom were playing with their toys in the living room. Lily had a big doll and Tom had a small car. They liked to make up stories with their toys and act them out.
