After lunch, they wanted to play with their toys again. But when they returned to the living room, they saw something strange. Their toys were not where they left them. Instead, they saw a big scale on the floor, with their toys on each side. The scale was balancing their toys, showing that the doll and the car weighed the same.

Lily and Tom were surprised and confused. They wondered who put their toys on the scale and why. They looked around and saw their dad smiling at them. He said, "Hi, kids. I saw your toys and I wanted to show you something. Do you know what this is?" He pointed to the scale.

Lily and Tom shook their heads. They did not know what a scale was. Their dad said, "A scale is a tool that can measure how heavy things are. It can tell you if something is heavier or lighter than something else. See, your doll and your car are the same weight. That means they are equal on the scale. But if I put something heavier on one side, like this book, the scale will tip. Watch." He put a book on the side with the doll and the scale tilted.

Lily and Tom watched with interest. They saw how the scale moved when their dad changed the weight on each side. They said, "Wow, that's cool. Can we try?"

Their dad said, "Sure, you can try. But be careful not to break the scale. It's fragile. And remember to put your toys back where they belong when you're done. OK?"

Lily and Tom said, "OK, dad. Thank you for showing us the scale. We learned something new today."

They took turns putting different things on the scale and seeing how it balanced or tipped. They had fun with the scale and their toys. They also remembered to return their toys to their places when they finished playing. They were happy and curious kids.

One day, Anna and Ben went to the market with their mom. They saw many fruits and vegetables that looked yummy and colorful. Anna liked apples and bananas, and Ben liked oranges and grapes. They asked their mom if they could have some, and she said yes.

But then, they saw a big green fruit that they did not know. It was an avocado. Anna and Ben were curious about it. They asked their mom what it was, and she said it was a fruit that some people liked to eat with salt and lemon. She said it was soft and creamy inside.

Anna and Ben wanted to try it. They asked their mom if they could have one, and she said yes. She gave them some money and told them to go to the man who sold the avocados. She said they had to pick a ripe one, not a hard one.

Anna and Ben went to the man who sold the avocados. They saw many avocados in a big basket. They did not know how to pick a ripe one. They decided to pull one at random. They pulled and pulled, but the avocado did not come out. It was stuck to the stem.

The man who sold the avocados saw them and got angry. He shouted at them and said they were ruining his avocados. He said they had to pay for the one they pulled. He said it was a terrible avocado, not ripe at all.

Anna and Ben were scared and sad. They did not have enough money to pay for the terrible avocado. They ran back to their mom and told her what happened. Their mom was disappointed and angry. She said they should have asked the man for help, not pull the avocados by themselves. She said they had to learn to be careful and respectful when they buy things.

She took them back to the man who sold the avocados and apologized to him. She paid for the terrible avocado and gave it to Anna and Ben. She said they had to eat it as a punishment. She said they would not like it, but they had to learn their lesson.

Anna and Ben peeled the terrible avocado and tasted it. It was hard and bitter and yucky. They did not like it at all. They wished they had picked a ripe one, or better yet, an apple or a banana. They learned their lesson. They said they were sorry to their mom and the man who sold the avocados. They said they would never pull avocados again.

Anna nods. Ben pushes the door. It opens with a loud creak. They go inside. They see a big bed, a big closet, and a big mirror. They also see a small box on a table.

"What is that?" Ben asks.

"I don't know. Do you want to open it?" Anna says.

Ben nods. He goes to the table. He picks up the box. He opens it. He sees a shiny ring. He puts it on his finger.

"Wow, look!" he says.

Anna goes to him. She sees the ring. She likes it. She wants it.

"Can I have it?" she asks.

"No, it is mine. I found it." Ben says.

He turns away. He looks at the mirror. He sees his face. But his face is not his face. It is an old face. It is a scary face. He screams.

Anna looks at the mirror. She sees Ben's face. But it is not Ben's face. It is an old face. It is a scary face. She screams.

They run to the door. They try to open it. But it is locked. They are trapped. They are scared. They cry.

The end.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They found a big box and a map. The map had pictures of animals and places. Lily and Ben wanted to see them.

"Let's go on an adventure!" Lily said. "We can use the box as a car and the map as a guide."

But when they got to the lion, they saw that he was very big and scary. He had sharp teeth and claws. He roared at them. Lily and Ben were afraid.

"Help!" Lily cried. "The lion is angry. He wants to eat us!"

"Quick!" Ben said. "Let's get out of here!"

They jumped out of the box and ran away. The lion chased them. They dropped the map on the ground.

"Let's go to the bird!" Lily said. "Maybe he can help us."

They got back in the box and drove to the bird. They made noises like a bird. Tweet, tweet!

But when they got to the bird, they saw that he was very small and shy. He had soft feathers and a beak. He hid in a tree. Lily and Ben tried to talk to him.

Tom thought for a moment. He liked all those flavors. He said, "Strawberry, please."

His mom smiled and pressed another button. The machine made a beep and a whir. Then, his mom took out the spoon with the medicine. It was still red, but it smelled like strawberries. She said, "Here you go, Tom. Try it now. It will taste like strawberries."

Tom was still a little scared, but he trusted his mom. He opened his mouth and took a sip of the medicine. It did taste like strawberries. It was sweet and yummy. He said, "Mmm, this is good. Thank you, mom. Thank you, machine."

His mom hugged him and said, "You're welcome, Tom. I'm glad you liked it. Now, you have to rest and drink some water. You will feel better soon."

Tom nodded and lay down on his bed. He felt a little warm, but he also felt happy. He had tasted something new and he had liked it. He closed his eyes and dreamed of strawberries.

It took one big step and jumped over the rock. The pony was so happy to be with its friends again. They all played together and had a fun day in the sun.

Once upon a time, there were two old friends. They were walking in the woods and were feeling brave. So, the two friends decided to march through the forest. 

As the two old friends marched, the forest started to look very different. The trunks of the trees were bigger, the leaves were darker and the birds were quiet. All of a sudden, the two old friends heard a big noise. It was a growl like they had never heard before. 

The forest felt dangerous. The old friends felt scared but they decided to keep marching. Then, they heard the noise again and saw a big animal in the distance. It was a bear! The bear was old, but it looked strong and ready to fight.

The old friends were so scared, but they knew they had to do something. They held hands and marched right up to the big bear. Then, the bear started to look friendly. It was happy to see them in the forest and even wanted to be their friend. 

The two old friends were so relieved that they started to laugh. They were no longer scared and all three of them started to march together. The bear, the old friends, and their new friendship marched until the sun went down.

Using her counting skills, she numbered each of the plants and flowers to see which were the most useful for the garden. After counting, she was able to find a few that could help bring the garden back to life!

The lily worked really hard and was soon able to find a way to help save the garden. All the animals and plants returned and it was as beautiful as ever. From that day on, the lily was known as the counting lily, because of her useful counting skills!

But Sally warned him, "Be careful, Timmy. We shouldn't take anything from nature."

Timmy didn't listen and took a handful of minerals. Suddenly, the ground shook and rocks fell from the cave ceiling. Timmy and Sally were trapped inside.

"Uh oh, what do we do now?" Timmy asked.

"We should have listened and respected nature," Sally replied sadly.

The moral of the story is to always respect nature and not take more than we need.

Suddenly, a voice called out. "Yes, I am here! I'm the Genie of the Chest." Peter was so excited! He asked, "What are you going to give me?"

The genie answered, "I will give you three wishes! But be careful what you wish for." Peter thought about it for a moment and then asked for a happy home. And that's exactly what he got!

So, although the chamber was dead, Peter left, feeling full of life, joy and love.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Jack. He looked at the beautiful blue sky and the pretty flowers in the garden, but something made him sad. He remembered the ugly plastic toys he had in the corner of his room.

Jack went inside and looked at the pile of toys. He touched them one by one, regretting that he didn't have something different to play with.

Suddenly, he heard a voice and looked up. It was his mother who said, "Jack, why don't you throw away those ugly plastic toys and get something nicer?"

Jack looked sadly at the toys and said, "I don't want to throw them away, Mom. They are my friends."

His mother smiled and said, "Well, then why don't you give them away to someone who will appreciate them more?"

Jack thought for a moment and then said, "Yes, that's a good idea. I will give them away so someone else can have fun with them." He quickly ran outside to find someone to give the toys away to.

Lily and Max were sad and angry. They did not want to resist. They wanted to go out. They started to cry and scream.

"Of course, my darling. We'll go out when the rain stops. I promise," Mom said.

One day, Tom and Polly saw a big dark cloud in the sky. It looked like a storm was coming. Polly was worried and said to Tom, "Tom, Tom, we should go back to the land. The storm is bad, it will make the sea angry and the wind strong. It will break your boat and hurt us."

Tom did not listen to Polly. He said, "Don't be scared, Polly. The storm is far away, it will not reach us. I like to sail on the sea, it is fun and exciting. You are a silly bird, you don't know anything about sailing."

Polly tried to warn Tom again, but he did not care. He sailed on, towards the storm. The storm got closer and closer, and the sea got rougher and rougher. The wind blew hard and the rain poured down. "Ow, this nut is too hard!" Ben said. He spit it out.

"See, you shouldn't have taken it from the squirrel," Lily said. "It's not for you."

"Fine, I don't want it anyway," Ben said. He threw the nut away.

They heard a beep from the kitchen. It was the timer.

"Come on, let's go see if the meat is ready," Lily said.

"Okay, maybe the meat is softer than the nut," Ben said.

They ran to the kitchen. Mom was taking the meat out of the oven. It smelled good.

"I will, Mom," Ben said.

Sara shook her head. She did not like those things in the soup. She only liked them by themselves. She wanted a sandwich and some juice. She crossed her arms and pouted.

Mom sighed. She knew Sara was stubborn. She had an idea. She got a blanket from the couch and wrapped it around Sara. She hugged her and said, "How about we pretend you are a little bear? And this is your cave. And this soup is your honey. Bears love honey, don't they?"

Sara smiled. She liked bears. She liked to pretend. She opened her mouth and let Mom feed her a spoonful of soup. She tasted it. It was not too hot and not too yucky. It was warm and sweet and soft. She liked it. She said, "Mmm, this is good honey. Thank you, Mom."

Mom smiled back. She was happy that Sara liked the soup. She said, "You're welcome, my little bear. I'm glad you tasted it. Now you can grow big and strong like a bear."

Sara nodded. She ate some more soup. She felt cozy and happy in her blanket. She was not stubborn anymore. She was a good little bear.

Lily loved to sing. She sang all day, in the morning, in the afternoon, and at night. She sang loud and high and low and soft. She sang happy songs and sad songs and funny songs. She sang to her dolls, to her cat, to her mom and dad.

One day, her mom said, "Lily, do you want to go to the opera with me? It is a place where people sing very well and wear pretty dresses and suits. It is very impressive."

Lily said, "Yes, yes, yes! I want to go to the opera! Can I wear a pretty dress too?"

Her mom said, "Of course, you can. Let me help you pick one."

They went to Lily's closet and found a pink dress with flowers and ribbons. Lily put it on and looked at herself in the mirror. She felt like a princess.

Her mom said, "You look beautiful, Lily. But you need one more thing. You need to tie your hair in a bun. That is how the singers at the opera do it. It makes them look elegant and neat."

Lily said, "But I don't know how to tie my hair in a bun. Can you do it for me?"

Her mom said, "I can, but I think you can learn how to do it yourself. It is not hard. You just need a comb, a rubber band, and a pin. Here, I will show you."

Her mom took Lily's hair and combed it back. She twisted it into a round shape and wrapped a rubber band around it. She secured it with a pin and said, "There, you did it. You tied your hair in a bun. How do you feel?"

Lily said, "I feel proud. I learned something new. Thank you, mom. You are the best."

Her mom said, "You are welcome, Lily. You are very smart and brave. Now, let's go to the opera and enjoy the music."

They went to the opera and sat in their seats. Lily saw the singers on the stage. They sang very well and wore pretty dresses and suits. They looked very impressive. Lily listened and watched with wonder. She clapped and cheered with the audience. She had a lot of fun.

She learned that the opera is a place where people sing very well and wear pretty dresses and suits. She also learned that she can tie her hair in a bun and look elegant and neat. She learned that she can do anything if she tries and listens and learns.

The moral of the story is: You can learn new things and have fun if you are curious and willing to try.

Tom does not listen to Mia. He runs to the bike and puts on the helmet. He feels mighty. He says, "I can ride the bike! I am not afraid!"

Mia runs to Tom and helps him up. She says, "Tom, are you okay? You should not have taken the bike! It was wrong and dangerous!"

Tom feels sorry. He says, "I am sorry, Mia. You were right. I was silly and greedy. I should have listened to you."

Mia says, "It is okay, Tom. I forgive you. But you have to say sorry to the owner of the bike too. And you have to be more careful next time."

Tom nods. He says, "I will, Mia. Thank you for being my friend."

Tom says, "I am sorry, sir. I took your bike without asking. I crashed it into a tree. I am very sorry."

The owner of the bike looks at Tom. He sees his knee is bleeding. He says, "Well, you are lucky you did not hurt yourself more. But you have to pay for the damage. And you have to learn to respect other people's things."

Tom says, "I will, sir. I learned my lesson. I will never do it again."

The owner of the bike says, "Good. Now go home and get some ice for your knee. And don't forget to wear a helmet next time you ride a bike."

Tom says, "I will, sir. Thank you."

Tom and Mia go home. They watch a movie and eat some cookies. They are happy. They are still friends.

Ben was scared and ashamed. He slid down from the zebra's back and ran to Lila. He said sorry to her and to the park ranger. He realized he was wrong and he should have listened to Lila.

The park ranger checked the statue and saw that it was not too damaged. He said to Ben and Lila, "You're lucky. This zebra is very important. It's a symbol of our park and our history. It's been here for a long time and we need to respect it and protect it. Do you understand?"

Ben and Lila nodded. They said they understood and they would never climb on it again. They asked the park ranger to tell them more about the zebra and why it was ancient. Lily thought that was great and wanted to explore the universe. She imagined herself zooming through space and seeing all the amazing things up there. But her mom told her that she couldn't go to the universe because it was too far away.

Lily was sad, but she kept dreaming about it. One night, she tried to build a rocket ship to zoom up to the universe. But it didn't work and she got hurt. She realized then that she couldn't go to the universe and that made her very sad.

Once upon a time, there was a big, fat cat named Whiskers. Whiskers loved to eat fish and sleep all day long. One day, while he was sleeping, a little mouse named Squeaky came to visit him.

"Hello, Whiskers! Wake up!" said Squeaky.

"What do you want, Squeaky?" asked Whiskers.

"I came to give you a lecture about sharing. You always eat all the fish and never split it with anyone," said Squeaky.

Whiskers thought about what Squeaky said and realized he was right. From that day on, Whiskers started to share his fish with Squeaky and they became good friends.

Benny said, "I regret starting this fort with you. You don't want to make it tidy." Lily felt sad and said, "I'm sorry, Benny. I just want to have fun."

Suddenly, it started to pour rain and Lily and her mom ran to find shelter under a tree. While they waited for the rain to stop, they ate their celery and talked about how much they loved it. Lily was scared and her feet hurt from walking on the rough ground. Rudy and Rosie offered to help her find her way home. "We can race to your house," said Rudy. "That way we can get there faster."

Lily was excited to race with the reindeer. She climbed on Rosie's back and the race began. Rudy and Rosie ran as fast as they could, jumping over logs and dodging trees. Lily laughed and held on tight.

Finally, they reached Lily's house and her parents were so happy to see her. "Thank you, Rudy and Rosie," said Lily. "You are the best reindeer ever!" From that day on, Lily and the reindeer would often race through the forest together, having lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a squirrel named Sammy. Sammy loved nuts and would collect them every day. One day, he found a big nut and was so excited to eat it. But he was too impatient to crack it open, so he buried it in the ground and ran away.

Days went by and Sammy forgot where he buried the nut. He searched and searched but couldn't find it. He realized that if he had just been patient and cracked the nut open, he could have enjoyed it right away instead of burying it and losing it forever.

The moral of the story is that it's important to be patient and not rush things. If we're too impatient, we might miss out on something great that's right in front of us.

Amy smiled and said, "Yes, you can help. We have more beans available." She gave Tom some beans and showed him how to cut them safely. They both worked together, cutting all the beans for their mom.

When they finished, their mom was so proud of them. She thanked Amy and Tom for their help and gave them a big hug. That night, the family enjoyed a delicious dinner with the beans that Amy and Tom had helped prepare.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim lived in a small house with his mom and dad. They were not rich, but they were very happy. Tim loved to help his mom and dad with chores around the house.

One day, Tim's mom asked him to help her pack a bag for a picnic. Tim was excited and said, "Yes, mom! I want to help!" They went to the kitchen and opened the fridge. Tim's mom took out some yummy food like apples, sandwiches, and juice. Tim carefully put the food in the bag.

At the picnic, Tim and his mom and dad laughed and ate the yummy food. They played games and had a lot of fun. When it was time to go home, Tim said, "I loved helping you pack, mom. Can we have another picnic soon?" His mom hugged him and said, "Of course, Tim. We can have more picnics because we have each other, and that makes us rich in love."

Sara and Tom were best friends. They liked to play in the park and look for shiny things. One day, they found a big diamond in the grass. It was very bright and pretty.

"Wow, look at this!" Sara said. "It must be worth a lot of money. Maybe we can be famous if we show it to someone."

Tom shrugged. He did not care about money or fame. He just wanted to play with Sara. "I don't know," he said. "Maybe we should leave it here. It might belong to someone else."

Sara shook her head. She wanted to keep the diamond. She put it in her pocket and ran to the street. "Come on, Tom," she said. "Let's go find someone who can tell us what it is."

Tom followed her, but he was worried. He did not like the street. It was noisy and crowded and dangerous. He saw a big car coming fast. He tried to warn Sara, but she did not hear him. She ran across the road, holding the diamond in her hand.

The car hit Sara. She fell to the ground. The diamond flew out of her hand and broke into pieces. Tom ran to her and cried. He wished they had never found the diamond. He wished they had stayed in the park and played. He wished Sara was still alive.

Sara and Ben were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big dog with black fur and a red collar. The dog was running and barking, and Sara and Ben wanted to pet it.

"Can we touch the dog, Mommy?" Sara asked.

"Only if the owner says it's okay, sweetie," Mommy said. "Some dogs are not friendly, and they might bite you."

Sara and Ben ran after the dog, but they did not see the owner. The dog stopped near a tree and looked at them. Sara reached out her hand to touch the fur, but the dog growled and showed its teeth.

"Rough, rough!" the dog said.

Sara was scared and pulled back her hand. She started to cry and scream. Ben was brave and tried to help his sister. He picked up a stick and waved it at the dog.

"Go away, bad dog!" Ben said.

The dog did not like the stick, and it barked louder and louder. It jumped at Ben and bit his arm. Ben felt a lot of pain and screamed too.

Mommy heard the screams and ran to the twins. She saw the dog and the stick and the blood. She was very angry and scared.

"Help, help!" Mommy shouted.

A man came running from the other side of the park. He had a leash in his hand. He was the owner of the dog.

"I'm so sorry, I'm so sorry!" the man said. "My dog is not used to children, he was just playing, he didn't mean to hurt them."

Mommy did not care what the man said. She hugged Sara and Ben and took them to the car. She drove them to the doctor, who gave them medicine and bandages.

Sara and Ben learned a lesson that day. They learned that they should not touch strange dogs, even if they look nice. They learned that they should listen to Mommy, who knows what is best for them. They learned that dogs can be rough, and that sticks can make them angry. They learned that screaming can help, but sometimes it is too late.

Tom and Mia like to play with their toys. They have many toys, but their favorite ones are the boats. They have big boats and small boats, red boats and blue boats, boats with sails and boats with motors.

One day, their mom says, "Tom and Mia, it is time to sort your toys. You have too many toys on the floor. Put them in the boxes, please."

Tom and Mia nod and start to sort their toys. They make a pile of boats and a pile of other toys. They are careful not to break their boats or lose any parts.

"Look, Mia, this is my best boat," Tom says, holding a big blue boat with a motor. "It can go very fast on the water. Do you want to try it?"

"Yes, please, Tom," Mia says, smiling. "This is my best boat," she says, showing him a small red boat with a sail. "It can go with the wind. Do you want to try it?"

They swap their boats and play with them for a while. They make boat noises and pretend they are sailing on the sea. They have fun with their boats.

"Tom and Mia, you did a good job sorting your toys," their mom says, coming back to the room. "Now you can put them in the boxes. The boats go in the blue box and the other toys go in the green box."

Tom and Mia put their boats in the blue box and their other toys in the green box. They are careful not to mix them up. They say goodbye to their boats and thank them for the fun.

"Can we play with our boats again tomorrow, mom?" Tom asks.

"Of course, you can, Tom," their mom says. "But now it is time for dinner. Come on, let's go."

Tom and Mia follow their mom to the kitchen. They are hungry and happy. They love their boats.

Lily and Sam are friends. They like to play in the park. Lily can hear and talk, but Sam cannot. Sam can see and sign. Sign is when you use your hands to say things.

One day, they see a big dog in the park. The dog is brown and soft. It has a long tail and a wet nose. Lily and Sam want to pet the dog, but they are scared. They do not know if the dog is nice or mean.

They look at the dog's owner. She is a lady with a red hat. She smiles and waves at them. She signs to Sam. She says, "Hello, my name is Anna. This is my dog, Coco. Coco is friendly. Do you want to pet him?"

Sam signs back to Anna. He says, "Hello, Anna. My name is Sam. This is my friend, Lily. Lily can hear and talk, but I cannot. I can see and sign. We want to pet Coco, but we are scared."

Anna nods and says, "I understand. Coco is a good dog. He likes children. He will not bite or bark. He will lick your face and wag his tail. You can pet him if you want. He is very soft."

Lily and Sam look at each other. They decide to try. They walk slowly to Coco. Coco wags his tail and sniffs them. He licks their hands and faces. He is very soft. Lily and Sam giggle and pet him. They are not scared anymore. They are happy.

They thank Anna and Coco. They say, "Bye, Anna. Bye, Coco. You are nice. We like you." Anna and Coco say, "Bye, Lily. Bye, Sam. You are nice. We like you too." They wave and smile. Lily and Sam go back to play. They have a new friend.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. Today, they see a big slide. It is bright red and yellow. Lily wants to go on the slide. She runs to the ladder.

"Come on, Tom!" she says. "Let's go on the slide!"

Tom is scared. He does not like high things. He stays on the ground.

"No, thank you," he says. "I don't want to go on the slide. It is too high."

Lily climbs up the ladder. She reaches the top. She looks down. She sees Tom. He looks small.

"Tom, you are missing the fun!" she says. "The slide is not scary. It is fun. You can do it!"

Tom shakes his head. He does not want to try. He sits on a bench. He watches Lily.

Lily slides down. She goes fast. She laughs. She feels happy. She lands on the grass. She gets up. She runs to the ladder again.

"Again, again!" she says. "I want to go on the slide again!"

Tom sees Lily. He sees her smile. He sees her laugh. He feels curious. He wonders what it is like to go on the slide. He stands up. He walks to the ladder.

"Lily, wait for me!" he says. "I want to go on the slide too!"

Lily is surprised. She is happy. She waits for Tom. She helps him climb up. They reach the top. They hold hands. They look at each other.

"Are you ready, Tom?" she says.

"Yes, I am ready, Lily," he says.

They slide down together. They go fast. They laugh. They feel happy. They land on the grass. They hug.

"That was fun, Lily!" he says.

"Yes, it was, Tom!" she says. "You did it! You are brave!"

They go on the slide again. And again. And again. They have fun. They are friends. They are happy.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to go to the market with Mom. The market has many things to see and smell and touch. Anna likes the fruits and Ben likes the toys.

One day, they see a man with a big wheel. The wheel has many colors and numbers. The man says, "Spin the wheel and win a prize!" Anna and Ben want to try. They ask Mom for a coin.

Mom gives them one coin each. Anna goes first. She spins the wheel hard. The wheel goes round and round and makes a noise. Anna hopes to get a big prize. The wheel stops on a red number. The man says, "You win a balloon! Choose your color!" Anna is happy. She picks a pink balloon. The man ties it to her wrist.

Ben is next. He spins the wheel harder. The wheel goes faster and faster and makes a louder noise. Ben hopes to get a bigger prize. The wheel stops on a green number. The man says, "You win a sticker! Choose your shape!" Ben is not happy. He does not want a sticker. He wants a balloon like Anna.

He says, "No, I want a balloon! Give me a balloon!" The man says, "Sorry, you can't change your prize. You have to take the sticker." Ben gets angry. He throws the coin at the man. He tries to grab Anna's balloon. Anna says, "No, Ben, this is my balloon! You can't have it!" They start to pull and tug on the balloon.

The balloon pops. It makes a loud bang. Anna and Ben are shocked. They start to cry. Mom comes over. She sees the broken balloon and the angry man. She says, "What happened? Why are you crying?" Anna and Ben tell her what they did. Mom is not happy. She says, "That was not nice. You have to say sorry to the man and to each other. You have to share and be happy with what you get." Anna and Ben say sorry. They hug each other. They take the sticker and the coin. They go to another stall. They see a lady with a big basket. The lady says, "Spin the basket and win a candy!" Anna and Ben look at each other. They smile. They ask Mom for another coin.

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to bake. They baked cookies, cakes, and pies with their mom. They used flour, sugar, eggs, and butter. They mixed, rolled, cut, and decorated. They put their treats in the oven and waited for them to be done.

One day, they wanted to bake something special for their dad. He was coming home from work soon. They asked their mom what he liked best. She said he liked gingerbread. Lily and Tom decided to bake a gingerbread house. They used cheap candy and frosting to make the roof, the windows, and the door. They used pretzels and marshmallows to make the fence and the chimney.

They were very proud of their gingerbread house. They put it on a big plate and carried it to the living room. They wanted to surprise their dad. They hid behind the couch and waited for him to come in.

Soon, they heard the door open and their dad's voice. "Hello, I'm home!" he said. He saw the gingerbread house on the table and smiled. He walked over to it and admired it. He saw the candy, the frosting, the pretzels, and the marshmallows. He saw the chimney and the smoke. He smelled the ginger and the spice.

He picked up a piece of the chimney and took a bite. He made a funny face and spit it out. He looked at the chimney again and saw something black and hard. He realized it was not candy, but coal. He wondered who put coal in the chimney.

Lily and Tom jumped out from behind the couch and giggled. They ran to their dad and hugged him. They said, "Surprise, dad! We baked you a gingerbread house! We used cheap candy and frosting, but we ran out of candy for the chimney. So we used coal instead. Do you like it?"

Their dad laughed and hugged them back. He said, "I love it, my sweeties. You are very creative and thoughtful. Thank you for baking me a gingerbread house. But next time, please don't use coal for the chimney. It tastes very bad and it makes me cough. Let's use chocolate or licorice instead. OK?"

Lily and Tom nodded and said, "OK, dad. We're sorry we used coal. We didn't know it was bad. We just wanted to make the chimney look real. We love you, dad."

They all smiled and kissed. They ate the gingerbread house together, except for the coal. They threw the coal in the trash. They had a happy and yummy time.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to pass the ball to each other and catch it. They also liked to eat apples that their mom gave them.

One day, a big dog came to the park. It saw Tom and Lily's ball and wanted to play too. It ran to them and took the ball in its mouth. It ran away with the ball.

Tom and Lily were sad and angry. They wanted their ball back. They chased the dog, but it was too fast. It went to a deep pond and jumped in. It swam with the ball.

Tom and Lily stopped at the edge of the pond. They could not swim. They did not know what to do. They saw the dog with the ball in the water. They shouted at the dog, but it did not listen.

Then, they saw a man with a big stick. He was the dog's owner. He called the dog and threw the stick in the pond. The dog dropped the ball and went after the stick. The ball floated to the shore.

Tom and Lily ran to the ball and grabbed it. They were happy and relieved. They thanked the man and hugged the ball. They decided to share their apples with the dog. The dog came out of the pond and wagged its tail. It liked apples too. They all became friends.

Lily was a furry cat who liked to play with her toys and eat her food. She was very happy with her family, who gave her lots of love and cuddles. But one day, Lily felt sick and did not want to play or eat. She only wanted to sleep and hide under the bed.

Her family was worried and took her to the vet. The vet was a nice lady who wore a white coat and had a big bag of tools. She said hello to Lily and tried to pet her, but Lily was scared and hissed. The vet said, "Don't worry, Lily, I just want to help you. I need to weigh you and take an x-ray of your tummy. That will tell me what is wrong with you."

The vet put Lily on a scale that beeped and showed a number. She said, "Oh, Lily, you are very thin. You have lost a lot of weight. That is not good." Then she took Lily to a dark room with a big machine. She said, "This is the x-ray. It will take a picture of your bones and organs. It will not hurt, but you have to stay still for a few seconds." She put Lily on a table and covered her with a blanket. She pressed a button and the machine made a buzzing sound.

The vet looked at the picture that came out of the machine. She frowned and shook her head. She said, "Oh, Lily, I'm sorry, but you have a big tumor in your tummy. That is why you are sick and in pain. It is too big and too bad to remove. There is nothing I can do to make you better."

Lily did not understand what the vet said, but she felt very sad and afraid. She wanted to go home and be with her family. She wanted to play and eat and be happy again. But she knew that she would not. She knew that she was going to die. She closed her eyes and wished for a miracle. But no miracle came.

Bella was a dog who liked to run and play with her friends. She had a soft fur and a long tail. She was happy and kind to everyone.

One day, she met a new dog in the park. His name was Rex and he had a short fur and a big mouth. He was not happy and kind. He was rude and mean.

"Hello, I am Bella. Do you want to play with me?" Bella asked Rex.

"No, I don't. You are too small and silly. Go away!" Rex barked at Bella.

Bella felt sad and hurt. She did not understand why Rex was so rude. She wanted to be his friend.

She saw that Rex had a ball in his mouth. She thought maybe he would like to share it with her.

"Can you lend me your ball for a little while? I will give it back to you soon. Please?" Bella asked Rex.

"No, I won't. This is my ball and you can't have it. It is mine, mine, mine!" Rex growled at Bella.

He bit the ball hard and made it pop. He did not care that he broke his ball. He only cared that Bella could not have it.

Bella was shocked and scared. She ran away from Rex. She did not want to play with him anymore. He was too rude and mean.

As she ran, she felt something itchy on her fur. She stopped and looked. She saw a tiny bug on her fur. It was a flea. It had jumped from Rex to her.

"Yuck! A flea! How did you get here?" Bella said to the flea.

"I came from Rex. He has many fleas. He does not wash or brush his fur. He is dirty and smelly. He is not nice to us either. He is rude and mean." The flea said to Bella.

Bella felt sorry for the flea. She did not like fleas, but she did not like rude and mean dogs either.

"Maybe you can find a better home. Do you want to jump to another dog?" Bella asked the flea.

"Yes, I do. Thank you for being kind to me. You are a good dog. Goodbye!" The flea said to Bella.

The flea jumped to another dog who was clean and friendly. Bella was happy for the flea. She hoped he would find a good home.

She also hoped that Rex would learn to be nice and share. She did not want to be his friend, but she did not want him to be lonely and unhappy.

She decided to go and find her other friends who were happy and kind. She wanted to play and have fun with them. She forgot about Rex and his ball. She was happy and kind.

Lily and Max were at the beach with their mom and dad. They liked to play in the sand and splash in the water. They also liked to look for shells and crabs and fish.

One day, they saw a big boat on the water. It had a net and a flag and a horn. The boat was catching shrimp, mom said. Shrimp were small and pink and tasty. Lily and Max wanted to see the shrimp.

They asked mom and dad if they could go to the boat. Mom and dad said yes, but they had to wear life jackets. Life jackets were bright and orange and fluffy. They made Lily and Max float and stay safe.

They put on their life jackets and walked to the boat. A man with a hat and a beard was on the boat. He smiled and waved at them. He said, "Hello, little ones. Do you want to see the shrimp?"

Lily and Max nodded and said, "Yes, please!"

The man showed them the net full of shrimp. They were wriggling and jumping and shining. Lily and Max touched them and counted them and said, "Wow!"

The man gave them each a shrimp to take home. He said, "These are for you. You can cook them and eat them or keep them as pets. They are very smart and friendly."

Lily and Max thanked the man and said, "Bye-bye!"

They ran back to mom and dad with their shrimp. They were very happy and excited. They decided to keep them as pets and name them Pinky and Sparky. They made a home for them in a bucket with water and sand and seaweed. They fed them and played with them and loved them. They were the best shrimp ever.

Lily and Ben are playing on the farm. They like to see the animals and help their grandpa. Grandpa has a big truck that he uses to send hay to other farms. Lily and Ben want to ride in the truck with him.

"Can we go with you, grandpa?" Lily asks.

"Sure, but you have to be careful. The truck is very bumpy and the hay is very messy. You don't want to get hurt or dirty," grandpa says.

Lily and Ben nod and climb into the truck. They sit on a big pile of hay and hold on tight. Grandpa starts the truck and drives away.

The truck goes fast and makes a lot of noise. Lily and Ben laugh and wave to the cows and the horses. They see the fields and the trees and the sky. They feel the wind and the sun on their faces.

The truck stops at another farm. Grandpa gets out and talks to a man. The man has a big fork and starts to take the hay from the truck. Lily and Ben watch him.

"Look, he is making a big stack of hay," Lily says.

"Maybe he has a lot of animals to feed," Ben says.

"Or maybe he likes to make hay forts," Lily says.

They giggle and imagine playing in the hay forts. They think it would be fun.

Grandpa comes back and gets into the truck. He smiles at Lily and Ben.

"Did you have a good ride?" he asks.

"Yes, grandpa, it was fun. Thank you for letting us go with you," Lily and Ben say.

"You're welcome, my dears. But now we have to go back. And you have to brush off the hay. You are very messy," grandpa says.

Lily and Ben look at each other and see the hay in their hair and clothes. They laugh and start to brush off the hay. They don't mind being messy. They had a great adventure.

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to go to the lake with their dad. Their dad was a fisherman who knew how to catch big fish. He taught them how to use a rod and a hook and a worm.

One day, they saw a thin man on the other side of the lake. He had a big net and a bucket. He was throwing the net into the water and pulling out many fish. Lily and Tom were curious and wanted to see what he was doing.

They asked their dad if they could go talk to him. Their dad said yes, but he told them to be careful and to trust him. He said he would watch them from the shore.

Lily and Tom walked around the lake until they reached the thin man. They said hello and asked him about his fish. The thin man smiled and showed them his bucket. He said he had many fish for his family and his friends. He said he liked to share his fish.

Lily and Tom thought he was nice and asked him if they could try his net. The thin man said yes, but he told them to be careful and to trust him. He said he would help them with the net.

Lily and Tom took the net and threw it into the water. They felt something heavy and tried to pull it back. But the net was stuck on something. They could not move it. They started to cry and to call their dad.

The thin man laughed and said he was sorry. He said he had tricked them. He said he had tied the net to a big rock. He said he wanted to keep all the fish for himself. He said he did not like to share his fish.

Lily and Tom were scared and angry. They wished they had not trusted the thin man. They wished they had stayed with their dad.

Their dad heard them and ran to them. He saw the thin man and the net and the rock. He was mad and he shouted at the thin man. He said he was a bad fisherman and a bad person. He said he should be ashamed of himself.

He untied the net and freed Lily and Tom. He hugged them and said he was sorry. He said he was proud of them for being brave and kind. He said he loved them and he would always protect them.

Lily and Tom hugged their dad and said they were sorry. They said they loved him and they would always trust him. They said they did not want to talk to the thin man anymore.

Lily and Ben were playing in the backyard. They had a big bucket of water and some plastic cups. They pretended to be chefs and made soup with water, leaves and flowers.

"Here, try my soup," Lily said, handing Ben a cup. "It's perfect."

Ben took a sip and made a face. "Yuck, it's too sour. I don't like it."

Lily felt sad. She worked hard on her soup. She wanted Ben to like it. She thought of a way to make it better.

"I know, I'll add some sugar. Wait here, I'll be right back," she said, running to the kitchen.

She found the sugar jar on the counter. She climbed on a chair and reached for it. But she was too small. She knocked over the jar and it fell on the floor. Sugar spilled everywhere.

"Oh no, what a mess!" Lily said. She heard her mom coming. She was afraid of getting in trouble. She ran back to the backyard.

But she forgot to turn off the faucet. Water started to flow out of the bucket. It made a big puddle on the grass. It reached the flower bed. It soaked the roses.

"Help, help!" the roses cried. "We're drowning!"

Ben heard the roses. He saw the water. He knew what to do. He grabbed the bucket and poured the water back into the faucet. He turned off the faucet. He saved the roses.

"Thank you, thank you!" the roses said. "You rescued us!"

Lily came back and saw what Ben did. She felt sorry for making a mess. She hugged Ben.

"I'm sorry, Ben. I was trying to make my soup better. But I made a big mistake. Can you forgive me?" she said.

His mom said, "Because they are different from us. They have wings and we have claws. They have feathers and we have fur. They have a different way of living and we have to let them be. The man saw Tom's helicopter. He said, "What a nice helicopter! Can I see it?" Tom said, "No, this is mine. I like it very much." The man said, "But I have something better for you. Look at this!" He took out a big, shiny helicopter from his bag. It had lights and sounds and a remote control. He said, "This is a special helicopter. It can do many things. It is not ordinary. Do you want to trade?"

Tom looked at the big helicopter. It was very pretty. He wanted to try it. But he also loved his toy helicopter. He remembered how he played with it every day. He said, "No, thank you. I don't want to trade. My helicopter is special to me. It is not ordinary either. It is my friend."

The man said, "Are you sure? You are missing a great deal." Tom said, "Yes, I am sure. Please go away." The man shrugged and put the big helicopter back in his bag. He said, "OK, suit yourself. Goodbye." He left with his bag of toys.

Tom hugged his toy helicopter. He said, "Don't worry, I will never sell you. You are the best helicopter in the world." He made it fly in the air and make loud noises. He smiled and went on another adventure.

Mia and Ben are friends. They like to play with toys. Mia has a big doll. Ben has a fast car. They share their toys and have fun.

One day, a new boy comes to their school. His name is Sam. He has many toys. He has a big truck, a loud plane, a shiny robot and more. He does not share his toys. He says they are his and only his.

Mia and Ben want to play with Sam. They ask him nicely. "Can we play with your truck, Sam?" Mia says. "Can we play with your plane, Sam?" Ben says. But Sam says no. He says they are too small and too silly. He says his toys are better than theirs. He laughs at them.

Mia and Ben are sad. They think Sam is mean. They go back to their toys. They play with the doll and the car. They have fun.

Sam sees them. He wants to play with them. He brings his robot. He says, "Look at my robot. It is cool. It can talk and dance. Do you want to play with it?" He tries to give it to Mia.

But Mia says no. She says, "No, thank you, Sam. We do not want to play with your robot. We like our toys. They are fun. You are not fun. You are spoiled. You do not share. You are not nice. Go away."

Sam is surprised. He is angry. He says, "Fine. I do not need you. I have my toys. They are the best. You are the worst." He takes his robot and goes away.

Mia and Ben smile. They hug their toys. They are happy. They are friends.

They took some cloths and rubbed the things hard. They made them sparkle and glitter. They put them on and pretended to be kings and queens. They said, "We are rich and powerful. We can do whatever we want."

But they did not know that the sack belonged to their dad. He had borrowed it from a museum for his work. The things were very old and valuable. They were not toys. They were dangerous. Some of them had sharp edges and could hurt them. Some of them had germs and could make them sick. Some of them had secrets and could cause trouble.

Their dad came home and saw them playing with the sack. He was very angry and scared. He said, "What are you doing? These are not yours. These are not for playing. These are for studying. You could have damaged them or hurt yourselves. You could have lost them or stolen them. You have to give them back right now."

Ben and Tom were very sorry and ashamed. They did not know they had done something wrong. They said, "We are sorry, dad. We did not know. We just wanted to have fun. We thought they were toys. We will not touch them again."

Their dad hugged them and said, "I forgive you, but you have to learn a lesson. You have to respect other people's things. You have to ask before you take something. You have to be careful with what you find. You have to know the difference between toys and treasures. Toys are for playing. Treasures are for keeping."

But then, the dish on Tom's head wobbled and fell off. It crashed on the floor and broke into many pieces. Tom and Lily heard a loud noise and stopped. They looked at the broken dish and felt very sad.

"I don't know, Lily, I'm sorry too," Tom said. He felt bad and guilty. He wished he had not played with the dish.

Lily and Tom were playing in the garden. They liked to look at the plants and smell the flowers. Lily saw a big plant with red and yellow leaves. She wanted to touch it.

"Look, Tom, what a pretty plant!" she said. "Can I touch it?"

Tom shook his head. "No, Lily, don't touch it. It is a bad plant. It can hurt you."

Lily did not listen to Tom. She reached out her hand and touched the plant. She felt a sharp pain in her finger. She cried out loud.

"Ow, ow, ow! It hurts, it hurts!"

Tom ran to her and saw her finger. It had a small dot of blood. He took her hand and said, "I told you not to touch it, Lily. It is a thorn plant. It has sharp things that can poke you. Come, let's go to Mom. She can make it better."

They ran to the house and found Mom in the kitchen. She saw Lily's finger and said, "Oh, my poor baby. What happened?"

Lily told her what happened. She said she was sorry for not listening to Tom. Mom cleaned her finger and put a band-aid on it. She gave her a hug and a kiss.

"There, there, Lily. It will be okay. Next time, listen to Tom. He knows what plants are good and what plants are bad. And don't touch any plant you don't know. Some plants can make you sick or uncomfortable."

Lily nodded. She said thank you to Mom and Tom. She learned her lesson. She decided to only look at the plants and not touch them. She and Tom went back to the garden and played with the toys. They had fun and were careful.

Lila showed him. She stood on one spot and turned around and around. She felt dizzy and happy. She laughed.

"Wow, that looks fun," Tom said. "Can I try?"

"Sure," Lila said. "But be careful. Don't spin too fast or you will fall down."

Tom tried to spin. He turned around and around. He felt dizzy and happy. He laughed.

But he spun too fast. He lost his balance and fell down. He bumped his head on the ground. He cried.

"Ow, ow, ow," Tom said. "My head hurts."

Lila ran to him. She hugged him and said, "I'm sorry, Tom. Are you okay?"

"Okay," Lila said. "Do you want to go to the tunnel?"

Tom looked at the tunnel. He thought for a moment and said, "Yes, let's go to the tunnel. The tunnel is not boring. It's safe and cozy and has nothing to hurt us."

Lila smiled and said, "Okay, let's go to the tunnel. Maybe we will find something to see."

They held hands and walked to the tunnel. They crawled inside and explored. They found a spider, a rock and a feather. They had fun. They forgot about spinning. They liked the tunnel.

He tried and tried, but it was too hard. He was about to give up, when he saw a key on the ground, at the bottom of the door.

Billy picked up the key and put it in the keyhole. He stepped back and watched as the door slowly opened.

He stepped inside and saw a new world filled with excitement and adventure! Billy was so excited, he couldn't believe his eyes.

The End.

The little girl smiled and replied, "Sure! I love jokes."

The friendly frog suggested a silly joke, "What do you call a frog who lives in the rain?" The little girl cocked her head to the side and thought for a moment. Then the frog said, "A po-toad-o!"

The little girl laughed and clapped her hands. She thought it was the funniest joke ever! She asked the frog if he knew another one.

The friendly frog happily shared more jokes with the little girl. They laughed and laughed until the sun set behind the trees. When it was time to go home, the friendly frog said goodbye with a friendly hop and a wave. 

The little girl waved back and put her fingers to her lips, "Shh! Don't tell anyone, but you're the best joke-teller ever!" The friendly frog smiled and watched her as she skipped away.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Tom. Tom was very worried because the water in the river behind his house was increasing. Tom thought it would reach his house soon and he wouldn't know what to do.

One day, Tom asked his mom what he could do about this. She said to him: "Tom, I know you are worried, but why don't you try building a sand row at the top of the river? That might help keep the water back".

Tom thought this was a good idea. He made lots of sand rows right at the top of the river. He used a bucket to transfer the sand from the beach to the top of the river. It was tiring but he knew it was important.

After a few hours, Tom saw that the water had stopped increasing! He was so happy that his hard work had paid off. He was now not so worried anymore. 

Tom smiled and said to his mom: "Thank you for your advice. Building the sand rows worked!"

One day, Lily and Sam wanted to show their mom their chess skills. They asked dad to set up the board and the pieces on the table. Then they took turns to move their pieces and try to catch the other's king.

"Look, mom, I moved my queen here. Now I can take Sam's rook!" Lily said, pointing to the board.

"Good move, Lily. But be careful, Sam might have a trick up his sleeve," mom said, smiling.

Sam looked at the board and saw a way to escape. He moved his king to a safe square and said, "Ha, you missed it, Lily. Now I can take your queen!"

He reached for Lily's queen, but Lily stopped him. She said, "No, you can't. That's a bad move. You have to follow the rules."

"What rules?" Sam asked, confused.

"The rules of chess, silly. You can't move your king into check. That means you can't put your king where my piece can take it. See, my bishop can take your king if you move it there. So you have to move it somewhere else," Lily explained.

Sam looked at the board again and saw that Lily was right. He felt sad and angry. He said, "That's not fair. You always know the rules better than me. You always win. You're a harsh player."

He pushed the board and the pieces fell on the floor. Lily and mom gasped. Dad came to see what happened.

"What's going on here?" he asked.

"Sam ruined the game. He made a bad move and then he got mad and threw the pieces," Lily said.

"Sam, why did you do that? That's not how you play chess. That's not how you display good manners. You have to respect the game and your opponent. You have to learn from your mistakes and try again. You have to say sorry to Lily and mom and help me pick up the pieces," dad said.

Sam felt ashamed. He knew dad was right. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I'm sorry, mom. I'm sorry, dad. I was a bad sport. I want to play chess again, but I need to learn the rules better. Can you help me, dad?"

Dad smiled and hugged Sam. He said, "Of course, I can help you, Sam. Chess is a fun and challenging game, but it also teaches you how to think and how to behave. I'm proud of you for apologizing and wanting to improve. Come on, let's pick up the pieces and set up the board again. And Lily, you did a great job too. You displayed your chess skills and your patience. Maybe you can teach Sam some tips and tricks."

Lily smiled and nodded. She said, "OK, dad. I'll help Sam. I like playing chess with him. He's my brother and my friend."

Mom watched them and felt happy. She said, "You're all wonderful. I love you all. Chess is a great game for our family."

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play in the garden. They have a big sandbox and a small pool. They also have a dog named Spot. Spot is brown and white and very friendly.

One day, Lily and Ben find a shiny coin in the sandbox. They are very happy. They show it to Spot. Spot likes shiny things. He barks and wags his tail.

"Let's buy something with the coin," Lily says.

"OK, what do you want to buy?" Ben asks.

Lily thinks for a moment. She sees a flower stand across the street. She likes flowers. They are pretty and smell good.

"I want to buy a flower for Mommy," she says.

"Me too," Ben says.

They hold hands and cross the street. They look at the flowers. There are many colors and shapes. They are all very nice.

"Hello, children," the lady at the stand says. "Do you want to buy a flower?"

"Yes, please," Lily and Ben say.

They give the lady the coin. The lady smiles. She gives them a cheap flower. It is yellow and small. It has a few petals and a green stem.

"Thank you," Lily and Ben say.

They go back to the garden. They show the flower to Spot. Spot sniffs the flower. He likes it. He licks it and rubs his head on it.

"Spot, no!" Lily and Ben say. "That's for Mommy!"

They take the flower from Spot. They see that the flower is wet and dirty. Some petals are gone. The stem is bent.

"Oh no," Lily and Ben say. "The flower is ruined."

They are sad. They wanted to give Mommy a nice flower. They think Mommy will not like the flower.

They hear Mommy calling them. She is coming to the garden. She wants to see what they are doing.

Lily and Ben hide the flower behind their backs. They hope Mommy will not see it.

"Hello, my sweeties," Mommy says. "What have you been playing with?"

Lily and Ben look at each other. They do not know what to say.

They decide to tell the truth. They show Mommy the flower. They tell her how they found the coin, bought the flower, and how Spot ruined it.

They say they are sorry. They say they love her.

Mommy looks at the flower. She looks at Lily and Ben. She smiles. She hugs them and kisses them.

She says she loves them too. She says the flower is beautiful. She says it is the best gift ever.

She says she does not care if the flower is cheap, or wet, or dirty, or missing petals. She says it is special because it came from them.

She says she will put the flower in a vase and keep it in her room.

Lily and Ben are happy. They smile and hug Mommy. They hug Spot too. They say he is a good dog.

They all go inside. They have a snack and a nap.

They dream of the garden and the flower.

Tom and Lily looked at each other and felt ashamed. They realized they were being mean and silly. They let go of the squash and said sorry to each other.

"Can we still have the squash for lunch?" Tom asked.

"Of course, but only if you cut it in half and share it nicely," mom said.

"Okay, mom," Tom and Lily said. They hugged each other and thanked the plant for the squash. They learned that sharing is better than fighting, and that the plant was a good friend that provided them with food.

Lila was a curious girl who liked to ask many questions. She wanted to know everything about the world. One day, she saw her mom baking a cake in the oven. She asked, "Mom, what are you doing?"

"I'm making a cake for your birthday, Lila. It's a surprise," her mom said.

"Can I help you?" Lila asked.

"Sure, you can help me complete the cake. But be careful, the oven is very hot. You don't want to touch it and get hurt," her mom said.

Lila nodded and followed her mom's instructions. She helped her mom mix the flour, the eggs, the sugar, and the milk in a big bowl. She helped her mom pour the batter into a round pan. She helped her mom put the pan in the oven. She helped her mom set the timer.

While they waited for the cake to bake, Lila asked her mom more questions. She asked, "Mom, why is the oven hot?"

"The oven is hot because it has heat inside. Heat makes things warm and sometimes changes them. Heat can make the batter turn into a cake, or make water turn into steam, or make ice turn into water," her mom explained.

Lila thought that was very interesting. She asked, "Mom, how does heat get inside the oven?"

"The oven has a part that makes heat. It's called an element. When we turn on the oven, the element gets hot and makes heat. The heat goes inside the oven and stays there until we turn it off," her mom said.

Lila nodded and smiled. She was happy to learn new things. She was also happy to help her mom complete the cake. She couldn't wait to see how it looked and tasted. She hoped it was yummy and pretty. But all of a sudden it started snowing. The little bird was so scared that he quickly flew lower and lower. "Oh no! Where did the sun go?" he said as he looked around.

But then he looked up and saw a rare and beautiful sight! A large rainbow was stretching across the sky! The little bird was so excited he flew up and started soaring through the rainbow.

"This is the best day ever!" he said as he flew higher and higher, enjoying the view and the warmth of the sun.

The little bird had such a wonderful day and he smiled all the way home. He knew he had experienced a rare and beautiful moment that he would never forget!

At first, Sally was very excited, she started jumping and singing around the house. 

But when they arrived at the beach, nobody was there and there was no dolphin. 

Sally was starting to get sleepy. Just when she was about to leave, she heard someone talking in the shore. It was a dolphin! 
 
The dolphin said: "Hi there, little girl. Do you want to be my friend?" 

Sally was so happy, she ran to the dolphin and gave it a big hug. They started swimming together and Sally was so very excited. In the end, she was so sleepy that she had to go home. 

But she always remembered her new friend, the dolphin.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to cook with her mom in the kitchen. One day, they were making pancakes. Lily's mom put a pan on the stove and poured the batter in. The pancakes turned out fluffy and brown.

Lily's dad came into the kitchen and said, "I have a joke for you, Lily. Why did the tomato turn red?" Lily giggled and said, "I don't know, why?" Her dad replied, "Because it saw the salad dressing!" Everyone laughed.

Later that day, Lily was playing with her toys when she heard a loud noise from the kitchen. She ran in and saw that the pan had caught on fire. Her parents were trying to put it out, but it was too late. The kitchen was destroyed.

The moral of the story is to always be careful in the kitchen and never leave a pan unattended on the stove.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing outside in the sunshine. One day, she saw a cricket hopping around in the grass. "Look, Mommy! A cricket!" she shouted with excitement.

Her mommy looked at the cricket and said, "Yes, crickets are very common in the summer. They make a chirping sound at night."

Lily wrinkled her nose and said, "Ew, that cricket is disgusting. It's so brown and has too many legs."

Mommy smiled and said, "Well, even though you think it's disgusting, crickets are important. They include many different species and help to keep the ecosystem balanced."

Lily thought about this for a moment and then said, "Okay, I guess crickets are important. But I still don't like them!"

After a while, the little girl's mom came looking for her and was surprised to see her daughter holding a fancy teddy bear. The little girl explained how Timmy gave it to her to hold until she found her own teddy bear. The mom was grateful and thanked Timmy for being such a kind kid.

From that day on, Timmy and the little girl became good friends and they would often play together at the park, holding their teddy bears tightly.

Once upon a time, there was a little duck named Ducky. Ducky lived in a pond with his friends. One day, Ducky decided to visit his friend, Bunny. Bunny lived in a big field with lots of carrots. 

Ducky waddled and quacked all the way to Bunny's field. When he got there, he saw Bunny playing with a rubber ball. Ducky wanted to play too, so Bunny let him play with the rubber ball. 

Suddenly, a big, scary dog came running towards them. Ducky was frightened and didn't know what to do. But Bunny was brave and chased the dog away. Ducky was grateful to Bunny for protecting him and they played with the rubber ball together until it was time for Ducky to go back to his pond.

Once upon a time, there was a wise owl who lived in a tree. One day, he met a little girl who was walking in the forest. She asked the owl, "What's your name?" The owl replied, "My name is Mr. Wise." 

The little girl said, "I want to see a volcano. Can you show me one?" Mr. Wise said, "Sure, but volcanoes are very dangerous. You have to be careful." 

They walked for a long time until they found a volcano. The little girl was happy, but then she got too close and fell into the volcano. Mr. Wise felt regret because he didn't warn her enough. 

He quickly flew down and saved the little girl. She was safe, but they both learned a lesson. The little girl learned to listen to wise advice and Mr. Wise learned to be more careful when showing dangerous things.

Red didn't know what to do. She wanted to believe the wolf but she remembered what her mom said. So, she ran as fast as she could to her grandma's house. When she got there, she told her grandma about the wolf.

Her grandma was smart and knew the wolf was up to no good. She told Red to never trust the wolf and to always be careful in the woods. From that day on, Red never saw the naughty wolf again.

Her mommy said, "That's right! You said it clear enough for me to understand. Good job!"

Her mommy smiled and said, "You remembered the word! You're such a smart girl." Lily felt proud of herself for remembering the word. From that day on, she loved watching the birds and learning new words.

As she climbed down, she noticed that the trunk of the tree was very hairy. She giggled and touched the hairy bark. Then, she said goodbye to the tree and skipped away, happy with her yummy prunes.

Her friend, a little monkey named Max, saw Ellie was sad and asked her what was wrong. Ellie showed Max her foot and Max saw the thorn. He told Ellie not to worry and went to find a thread to help remove the thorn.

Max came back with a thread and carefully removed the thorn from Ellie's foot. Ellie was so happy and thanked Max for helping her. From that day on, Ellie made sure to watch where she stepped so she wouldn't get hurt again.

As he was carving, he noticed a crazy looking bug crawling out of the squash. It scared him a little, but he didn't want to stop decorating. He continued carving until he made a face on the squash. 

That night, Timmy put the jack-o-lantern outside to scare his friends. But when they came over, they saw something even scarier. The crazy bug had multiplied and was now crawling all over the pumpkin. They ran away screaming and Timmy learned his lesson to always be careful when decorating.

Together, they looked all around the park. The angel flew up high to see better. At last, she found the toy under a big tree. The little girl was so happy, and they both played together. From that day on, the cheerful angel and the little girl became the best of friends.

Lily cried. She picked up her broken guitar and ran away. She said, "You are mean, Tom. You are not my friend anymore."

It was not weak. It was beautiful and precious. You played wonderful songs with it. You should be proud of your guitar and yourself."

He hugged her and said, "Don't worry. I will fix your guitar. And I will teach you more songs. And you will find better friends who will appreciate your guitar and your music. You are a great guitar player, Lily. And I love you very much."

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, dad. I love you too. And I love my guitar."

The moral value of the story is: You should respect and value the things that are important to others, even if they are different from yours. You should not judge or hurt others by their appearance or size. You should be kind and supportive of your friends and their talents. You should be grateful for the gifts and love that you receive.

They reached the edge of the hole and peered down. They saw nothing but blackness. Lily leaned forward, curious and brave. Ben held on to her, nervous and scared.

Suddenly, the ground shook and a loud roar came from the hole. Lily and Ben screamed and jumped back. They saw a huge head with sharp teeth and fiery eyes emerge from the hole. It was a dragon!

The dragon looked at them and snorted. It opened its mouth and breathed out a blast of fire. Lily and Ben ran away as fast as they could. They did not stop until they reached their houses.

They were safe, but they were also confused. How did a dragon become in the field? Where did it come from? Why did it attack them? They had many questions, but no answers.

They decided to never go near the hole again. They also decided to never tell anyone what they saw. They thought no one would believe them. They thought they might get in trouble.

They still played in the field, but they stayed away from the hole. They also stayed close to each other. They were still best friends, but they also had a secret. A secret that made them feel both excited and afraid. A secret that they would never forget.

Mom heard the noise and came into the kitchen. She was very angry and sad. She said, "What have you done? You ruined the cake and the fridge! You were not supposed to eat the cake now! You were not supposed to fight over it! You were supposed to share it!"

Mia tears off the ribbon and the paper. She opens the box. She gasps. Inside the box, there is another puppy. The puppy is unusual. He has brown and white spots all over his fur. He looks like Spot's brother.

Mia is overjoyed. She lifts the puppy out of the box and hugs him. She says, "Thank you, mom! Thank you, dad! He is so cute! What is his name?"

Mom and dad say, "His name is Dot. He is Spot's brother. We found him at the shelter. We thought you would like to have another puppy to play with."

Mia says, "I love him! I love you, Dot! I love you, Spot! I love you, mom and dad!"

Mia wraps her arms around Dot and Spot. They lick her face and wag their tails. Mom and dad wrap their arms around Mia and the puppies. They are a happy family.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom and Sam cried. "Help, help, help!"

A man who worked in the park heard their cries. He came and chased the ostrich away. He helped Tom and Sam with their scratches and bruises.

"Why did you try to touch the ostrich?" the man asked. "It is a wild animal. It does not like to be bothered."

"We were curious," Tom said. "We wanted to make friends with it."

"Well, you cannot make friends with an ostrich by touching it," the man said. "You have to respect its space and leave it alone. That is how you make friends with animals."

Tom and Sam learned their lesson. They said sorry to the ostrich and the man. They decided to play with their toys instead. They never bothered the ostrich again.

Once upon a time, there was a great big park with lots of trees and flowers. In the park, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play. One day, Lily saw a pigeon sitting on a bench.

"Hello, pigeon! What are you doing?" asked Lily.

"I am counting how many people are in the park today," replied the pigeon.

Lily was surprised. "Can pigeons count?" she asked.

"Yes, we can!" said the pigeon proudly. "I can count up to five."

"That's great!" said Lily. "I can count up to ten. Let's count together!"

So, Lily and the pigeon counted all the people in the park. They had so much fun counting together that they became good friends and counted everything they saw in the park.

Finally, Timmy's mom saw how uncomfortable he was and took a closer look. She saw a bug on his back! She quickly flicked it off and Timmy felt so much better. Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play with toys and books. One day, they go to the park with their moms. There is a big pond in the park. Anna and Ben see some ducks and fish in the pond.

"Look, Ben, the ducks can swim!" Anna says.

"I want to swim too!" Ben says.

"No, Ben, you can't swim in the pond. It is dirty and cold. And you don't have a swimsuit," Anna says.

"But I have glue!" Ben says. He takes out a bottle of glue from his backpack. He opens the cap and pours some glue on his arms and legs.

"What are you doing, Ben?" Anna asks.

"I am making a swimsuit with glue. Then I can swim like a duck," Ben says.

"That is silly, Ben. Glue is not a swimsuit. Glue is sticky and hard. It will not let you swim. It will make you stuck," Anna says.

But Ben does not listen to Anna. He runs to the pond and jumps in. He tries to swim, but he can't. The glue makes his arms and legs stick together. He feels cold and wet. He starts to cry.

"Help, help, I can't swim!" Ben shouts.

Anna and their moms hear Ben. They run to the pond. They see Ben in the water. He looks like a black ball of glue.

"Oh, Ben, what have you done?" Anna's mom says.

"Don't worry, we will get you out," Ben's mom says.

They pull Ben out of the pond. They take him to the bathroom. They wash off the glue with warm water and soap. They dry him with a towel. They give him some clean clothes.

"Ben, you are very lucky. You could have drowned in the pond. Glue is not a swimsuit. Glue is for making things stick, not for swimming," Ben's mom says.

"I am sorry, mom. I was silly. I wanted to swim like a duck," Ben says.

"Next time, if you want to swim, you have to ask us first. And you have to wear a real swimsuit. And you have to swim in a safe place, like a pool or a beach," Ben's mom says.

"OK, mom. I understand. Can I still play with Anna?" Ben asks.

"Of course, you can. But no more glue, OK?" Ben's mom says.

"OK, mom. No more glue," Ben says.

Anna and Ben hug. They are still friends. They go back to the park. They play with toys and books. They watch the ducks and fish in the pond. But they don't swim in the pond. They know better now.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys in their big room. They have many toys, but their favorite is a luxury train set. It has a brilliant red engine, a blue wagon, and a green caboose. It can make noises and move on the tracks.

One day, Sara and Ben are playing with the train set. Sara wants to be the driver of the engine. Ben wants to be the driver too. They both grab the engine and pull it.

"Let go, Sara! It's my turn!" Ben says.

"No, Ben! It's my turn!" Sara says.

They pull harder and harder. The engine starts to shake. Then, it breaks into two pieces. Sara and Ben are shocked. They drop the pieces and start to cry.

Mom hears the noise and comes to the room. She sees the broken engine and the crying twins. She is not happy.

"What happened here?" Mom asks.

"Sara and Ben broke the train!" They both say.

Mom sighs. She picks up the pieces and looks at them. She says, "This was a luxury train set. It was very expensive and special. You should not fight over it. You should share it and take care of it. Now, it is ruined. How do you feel?"

Sara and Ben feel sorry. They say, "We feel bad, Mom. We are sorry. We love the train. We love each other. We don't want to fight."

Mom smiles. She says, "I'm glad you are sorry. I love you too. Maybe we can fix the train. But first, you need to hug and say sorry to each other."

Sara and Ben hug and say sorry. They feel better. Mom hugs them too. She says, "Now, let's see if we can glue the train back together. And next time, remember to play nicely and take turns."

Sara and Ben nod. They say, "Yes, Mom. Thank you, Mom."

They help Mom glue the train. They hope it will work again. They promise to share it and take care of it. They think the train is still brilliant.

Sam and Tom were friends. They liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big red cap on a bench. Sam ran to get it.

"Look, Tom, I found a cap! It is so pretty and shiny!" Sam said.

Tom was not happy. He wanted the cap too. He said, "No, Sam, that is not your cap. It is mine. I lost it yesterday. Give it to me!"

Sam did not believe Tom. He said, "No, Tom, you are lying. This is my cap. I found it. Go away!"

Tom was angry. He pushed Sam and grabbed the cap. Sam fell down and hurt his knee. He cried.

A man came to the bench. He saw Tom with the cap and Sam on the ground. He said, "Hey, kid, what are you doing with my cap? That is not yours. Give it back!"

Tom was scared. He dropped the cap and ran away. The man picked up his cap and put it on his head. He said, "Thank you, Sam, for finding my cap. I am glad you did not take it. Are you okay?"

Sam was sad. He said, "I am sorry, mister. I thought it was a nice cap. I wanted to keep it. But Tom said it was his and he took it from me. He was mean to me."

The man said, "I am sorry, Sam. Tom was wrong to do that. He should not lie or hurt you. You should not fight over things that are not yours. You should be friends and share. Here, you can have this." He gave Sam a candy.

Sam smiled. He said, "Thank you, mister. You are kind. But I wish Tom was my friend again. I miss him."

The man said, "Maybe you can talk to Tom and say you are sorry. Maybe he will say he is sorry too. Maybe you can be friends again. But you have to be honest and nice to each other. Do you understand?"

Sam nodded. He said, "I understand. I will try. Thank you, mister. Goodbye."

Sam walked away with his candy. He hoped Tom would come back and play with him. But Tom did not come back. He was too ashamed and afraid. He lost his friend and the cap. He was not glad. He was sad.

Tim and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they discover a pond with fish and frogs. They want to swim with them.

"Can we swim, please?" Tim asks his mom.

"No, you can't. The pond is dirty and deep. You might get sick or drown. Stay away from it," his mom says.

But Tim and Mia are not patient. They wait until his mom is busy talking to another mom. Then they sneak to the pond. They take off their shoes and socks. They step into the water.

"Look, a fish!" Mia says. She tries to catch it with her hands.

"Look, a frog!" Tim says. He tries to touch it with his feet.

But the fish and the frog are fast. They swim away from them. Tim and Mia get angry. They splash each other with water. They laugh and scream.

They do not see the big snake that lives in the pond. The snake is hungry and angry. It sees Tim and Mia. It swims towards them. It opens its mouth. It bites Tim on his leg. Tim feels a lot of pain. He cries and bleeds.

Mia sees the snake. She is very scared. She runs out of the pond. She calls for help.

"Mom! Mom! Tim is hurt! There is a snake in the pond!"

His mom hears her. She runs to the pond. She sees Tim and the snake. She is very scared too. She tries to pull Tim out of the water. But the snake is strong. It does not let go of Tim. It pulls him deeper into the pond.

Tim's mom and Mia scream and cry. They cannot save Tim. The snake eats him. Tim is gone.

The big boy was scared. He knew the park keeper was in charge. He said, "Sorry, sorry. I will not do it again." He let go of the swing and ran away.

Tom and Anna were happy. They thanked the park keeper. She said, "You are welcome. You are very brave. You did not let the big boy hurt you. You can swing as long as you want." She smiled and went to check on the other kids.
