Bear was sad. He said, "But I am hungry. And I like honey. It is sweet and sticky. Please, can I have some honey?"

Bee thought for a moment. She said, "Well, maybe you can have some honey, if you help us. We need more flowers to make more honey. Can you plant some seeds for us?"

Bear nodded. He said, "Yes, I can plant some seeds for you. Where are the seeds?"

Bee gave him some seeds. She said, "Take these seeds and put them in the ground. Then water them and wait for them to grow. When they grow, they will have flowers. And we will have more honey."

Bear took the seeds. He said, "Thank you, Bee. I will plant the seeds for you. And then, can I have some honey?"

Bee smiled. She said, "Yes, then you can have some honey. But only a little bit. And you have to share with us."

Bear agreed. He said, "OK, I will share with you. Thank you, Bee. You are very kind."

Bee and Bear became friends. They helped each other. And they enjoyed the honey. It was sweet and sticky.

Lily and Max nod. They understand. But they don't want to clean up. They want to watch TV and have a snack. They think of a plan.

"Mom, can we show you something?" Lily says.

"Sure, what is it?" Mom says.

Lily and Max run to their closet. They bring out their puppy, Spot. Spot is adorable. He has brown fur and black spots. He wags his tail and licks Mom's face.

"Look, Mom. This is Spot. He is our new friend. We found him in the park. He was alone and hungry. Can we keep him, please?" Max says.

Mom is surprised. She loves animals. She feels sorry for Spot. But she also knows that having a puppy is a lot of work.

"Lily and Max, Spot is very cute. But you can't keep him. He belongs to someone else. Maybe he has a tag or a chip. We have to find his owner. And you still have to clean up your room. That's not fair to Spot either. He needs a clean and safe place to stay." Mom says.

Lily and Max are sad. They love Spot. They don't want to give him away. But they also know that Mom is right. They hug Spot and say sorry.

"OK, Mom. We will clean up our room. And we will help you find Spot's owner. Maybe we can visit him sometimes. He is our friend." Lily and Max say.

Mom smiles. She is proud of Lily and Max. They are good kids. They learn from their lecture. They hug Mom and Spot. Then they start to clean up their room.

"Look, Ben, I made a purple cat!" Lily said, showing her paper to her friend. "Do you like it?"

Ben nodded. He liked Lily's cat. But he did not like to paint. He liked to dig. He had a shovel and a bucket. He liked to make holes and piles of dirt.

"Can I paint with you, Lily?" Ben asked. He wanted to try something new.

"Sure, Ben, you can paint with me!" Lily said. She was happy to share her paints and brushes. She gave Ben a paper and a brush. "What do you want to paint?"

Ben looked at the paints. He saw red, blue, yellow, green, orange and purple. He did not know what to paint. He felt shy.

"I don't know, Lily. I'm not good at painting." Ben said. He put down the brush.

Lily took Ben's hand and picked up the brush. She dipped it in the yellow paint. She made a circle on the paper. "This is the sun, Ben. The sun is bright and warm. Do you like the sun?"

Ben nodded. He liked the sun. He smiled and said, "Yes, I like the sun. Can I make the sky?"

Lily nodded. She gave Ben the blue paint. Ben painted the sky around the sun. He liked how the colors looked together. He felt happy.

Lily and Ben continued to paint. They made a green grass, a red flower, an orange bird and a purple butterfly. They made a beautiful picture. They were proud of their work.

Lily and Ben smiled. They felt happy and proud. They had fun painting. They learned something new. They encouraged each other. They were good friends.

"Look, Ben, I made a boat!" Lily said. "Can you make one too?"

Ben tried to fold his paper like Lily, but it was hard. He got angry and tore his paper. Then he saw a knife on the table. He wanted to cut his paper and make a boat.

"No, Ben, don't touch the knife!" Lily shouted. "It is sharp and can hurt you!"

But Ben did not listen. He grabbed the knife and tried to cut his paper. He did not hold the knife right and cut his finger. He cried out loud and dropped the knife.

Mama heard Ben cry and ran to the room. She saw the blood on his finger and the knife on the floor. She was scared and angry.

"Ben, what did you do?" Mama asked. "Why did you touch the knife? You know it is not a toy!"

Ben was sorry and ashamed. He said, "I wanted to make a boat like Lily, but I could not fold the paper. I thought the knife would help me."

Mama hugged Ben and said, "I understand, but you should never touch the knife without asking me. It is very dangerous and can hurt you badly. Next time, you should be patient and ask me or Lily to help you fold the paper. Okay?"

Ben nodded and said, "Okay, Mama. I am sorry. I will be patient and careful next time."

Mama cleaned Ben's finger and put a bandage on it. She said, "It is okay, Ben. I love you. But you have to be more careful and listen to Lily. She is a good sister and knows how to fold paper well. Maybe she can teach you how to make a boat."

Ben smiled and said, "Thank you, Mama. I love you too. And I love Lily. Can we play with paper again?"

Mama said, "Yes, you can. But only with paper, not with the knife. And only after you say sorry to Lily and give her a hug."

Ben said, "Okay, Mama. I will say sorry to Lily and give her a hug. And then we can play with paper and make boats together."

Tom was a big boy who liked to step on things. He stepped on toys, he stepped on flowers, he stepped on bugs. He thought it was fun to make things flat and broken. He did not care if he hurt anyone or anything.

One day, he found a big ball in his yard. It was blue and green and had many pictures on it. It looked like a world. Tom wanted to step on it and see what would happen. He lifted his foot and got ready to smash the ball.

But then, he heard a voice. It was a soft and sad voice. It came from the ball. It said, "Please, don't step on me. I am the world. I have many living things on me. They are your friends. They need me to be happy and healthy. If you step on me, you will hurt them and me. You will make me ugly and sick. Please, be kind and gentle with me."

Tom was surprised. He did not know the ball could talk. He did not know the ball was the world. He did not know he had friends on the ball. He felt sorry for the ball. He put his foot down and looked at the ball. He saw the pictures of animals, plants, people, and places. He saw how beautiful and colorful they were. He saw how they needed the ball to live.

He said, "I'm sorry, world. I did not mean to hurt you. I did not know you were alive. I did not know you were my friend. I will not step on you. I will be kind and gentle with you. I will take care of you and your living things. I want you to be happy and healthy. I want you to be beautiful and bright."

The world smiled and thanked Tom. It said, "You are a good boy, Tom. You have a big heart. You can learn many things from me and my living things. You can have fun with them and share with them. You can make the world a better place. I am happy to be your friend."

Tom smiled and hugged the world. He felt happy and warm. He learned a big lesson that day. He learned to love and respect the world and all that was on it. He learned to not step on things, but to step with things. He learned to be a friend of the world.

When the man gave her the hot dog, she took a bite and it was very tasty. Her friend, Tommy, came up and said, "That hot dog looks attractive. Can I have one too?" Lily replied, "Sure, let's go get you one!" And off they went to get Tommy his own hot dog.

One day, Sara's friend Tom came to visit. Tom liked to run and jump and kick balls. He saw Lily sleeping on the couch and wanted to play with her. He ran to the couch and shouted, "Wake up, kitty! Let's play!"

Lily was scared and angry. She hissed and scratched Tom's hand. Tom was hurt and angry too. He kicked Lily off the couch and yelled, "Bad kitty! Go away!"

Sara saw what Tom did and was very sad and angry. She ran to Lily and hugged her. She said to Tom, "You are mean! Lily is my pet and you hurt her! She is delicate and you scared her! You can't kick her! You have to be gentle and nice!"

Tom felt sorry and ashamed. He said to Sara, "I'm sorry, Sara. I didn't know Lily was delicate and scared. I just wanted to play. I won't kick her again. Can we still be friends?"

Sara looked at Tom and saw that he was sorry. She said to Tom, "Okay, Tom. We can still be friends. But you have to be careful with Lily. She is my pet and I love her. Do you want to play with her toys instead?"

Tom nodded and smiled. He said to Sara, "Yes, Sara. I want to play with her toys. They look fun. Can I pet Lily too?"

But she was afraid that Anna would hate her and not be her friend anymore. She was afraid that everyone would call her a thief and a liar. She was afraid that her mom would be disappointed and angry with her. She did not know what to do.

Anna looked at her with tearful eyes and said, "Thank you, Lily. You are my best friend. You have a big heart and you are always humble and helpful. I love you."

She knew she had lost her heart. She wished she had never found the necklace. She wished she had listened to her mom. She wished she had been honest and kind. But it was too late. She had made a big mistake. And she had to live with it.

"OK, Ben, Lily. Let's go home. I love you," Spot said, and followed them.

Lily was a smart girl who liked to learn new things. She had a meeting with her teacher today to show her what she had learned. She was very excited and wanted to be on time.

But on the way to school, she saw a big red truck with a loud siren. It was a fire truck and it was going to help someone. Lily loved fire trucks and wanted to see where it was going. She followed the fire truck and forgot about her meeting.

She saw the fire truck stop at a house that had smoke coming out of it. She saw the firefighters get out and spray water on the fire. She saw the people who lived in the house come out and hug each other. She thought it was very brave and kind of the firefighters to help them.

She was so busy watching that she did not notice the time. She looked at her watch and saw that she was very late for her meeting. She felt sorry and ran back to school.

She got to her teacher's office and knocked on the door. She saw her teacher sitting at her desk with a frown on her face. She said, "I'm sorry, teacher, I was delayed by a fire truck. I wanted to see what they were doing."

Her teacher looked at her and said, "Lily, I'm glad you are safe, but you should not follow fire trucks. They are very dangerous and you could get hurt. And you should not delay your meeting. It is rude and disrespectful to make someone wait for you. You are a smart girl, but you need to be responsible and respectful too. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, teacher, I understand. I'm sorry I delayed you. I won't do it again. Can I still show you what I learned?"

Her teacher smiled and said, "Of course, Lily. I'm happy to see what you learned. But next time, please be on time and don't follow fire trucks."

Lily said, "Thank you, teacher. I learned my lesson. I will be on time and respectful from now on."

The moral of the story is: Don't follow fire trucks and don't delay your meeting. Be responsible and respectful.

Tim's mom was happy that he did not touch the knife. She said, "Good job, Tim! You are a smart boy." She cut the cake and gave Tim a big piece. They ate the cake together and had a great day. From that day on, Tim always listened to his mom and stayed away from the knife.

Sara loved crabs. She wanted to see it. She put down her shell and went to Ben's bucket. Ben smiled. He was going to send the crab to Sara and make her scream. Then he would take her shell.

But the crab did not like being in the bucket. It wanted to go back to the water. It saw Sara's hand and pinched it hard. Sara screamed and dropped the bucket. The crab ran away. Sara was hurt and scared. She cried.

Ben felt bad. He saw that his plan was mean and wrong. He hurt Sara and the crab. He did not want the shell anymore. He wanted to say sorry to Sara.

"I am sorry, Sara. I was jealous of your shell. I tried to send the crab to you and make you scream. That was not nice. Are you okay?" he said.

Sara was still crying, but she heard Ben. She saw that he was sorry. She forgave him.

"It is okay, Ben. I am sorry too. I did not want to share my shell. That was not nice either. We can be friends again," she said.

They hugged and made up. They learned that being jealous and mean is not good. They learned to share and be kind. They played on the beach again and had fun. They found more shells and crabs and showed them to each other. They were happy.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Lily had a doll with a pretty dress and long hair. Ben had a car with big wheels and loud noises. They were having fun, but they wanted to try each other's toys.

"Can I play with your car, Ben?" Lily asked.

"Can I play with your doll, Lily?" Ben asked.

They agreed to swap their toys for a little while. Lily took the car and made it zoom around the floor. Ben took the doll and brushed her hair. They were happy, until they saw a match on the table.

"Look, a match!" Lily said. "We can make fire!"

"No, Lily, that's bad!" Ben said. "Fire is hot and dangerous!"

But Lily did not listen. She grabbed the match and tried to strike it on the table. Ben tried to stop her, but it was too late. The match lit up and burned Lily's finger. She dropped the match and the car. The car caught fire and melted. Lily cried and Ben cried.

"Mommy, Daddy, help!" they shouted.

Mommy and Daddy came running. They saw the fire and the smoke. They grabbed a blanket and put out the fire. They checked Lily's finger and Ben's doll. Lily's finger was red and sore. Ben's doll was ugly and burned.

Mommy and Daddy were angry and sad. They scolded Lily and Ben for playing with matches. They told them to never do that again. They threw away the match and the car and the doll. They hugged Lily and Ben and gave them some ice and a band-aid.

Lily and Ben felt sorry and ashamed. They said sorry to Mommy and Daddy. They said sorry to each other. They thanked Mommy and Daddy for helping them. They learned their lesson. They decided to play with safer toys. They promised to be careful and share. They were still friends.

Ben and Lily were playing at the beach with their buckets and shovels. They liked to dig holes and make sand castles. They saw a big boat on the water. It was white and shiny. It had a flag and a horn.

"Wow, look at that boat!" Ben said. "It is a yacht. It is very big and pretty."

"I want to go on the yacht," Lily said. "Maybe they have toys and snacks on it."

They ran to the edge of the water and waved at the yacht. They hoped someone would see them and invite them on board. But the yacht did not stop. It sailed away, leaving a trail of bubbles behind.

Ben and Lily were sad. They wanted to play on the yacht. They went back to their sand castles and tried to cheer up.

"Hey, I have an idea," Ben said. "Let's make our own yacht. We can use our buckets and shovels and some shells and sticks."

"OK, that sounds fun," Lily said. "How do we make a yacht?"

Ben showed her how to make a big mound of sand and shape it like a boat. He used a stick for a mast and a shell for a flag. He dug a hole for a cabin and put some pebbles inside. He made a horn out of a cone-shaped shell and blew on it.

"Look, we have a yacht!" Ben said. "It is mighty and loud. We can pretend to sail on it and have adventures."

Lily liked the yacht. She climbed on it and pretended to steer it. She used another shell as a telescope and looked around.

"Ahoy, matey!" she said. "I see an island with palm trees and monkeys. Let's go there and find treasure."

"OK, let's go!" Ben said. He blew the horn and they pretended to sail away.

They had a lot of fun on their yacht. They did not mind that it was made of sand. They used their imagination and had a great time. They did not see the big wave that came and washed away their yacht. They only heard a splash and felt the water on their feet.

"Hey, where did our yacht go?" Ben said. He looked around and saw only sand and water.

"Oh no, our yacht is gone!" Lily said. She was sad. She liked their yacht.

They looked for their yacht, but they could not find it. It was buried under the water. They felt like crying.

"Maybe we can make another one," Ben said. He tried to be brave.

"Maybe," Lily said. She sniffed.

They hugged each other and walked back to their buckets and shovels. They decided to make something else. Maybe a castle or a car or a rocket. They still had their imagination and their fun. They did not need a real yacht. They had each other.

One day, a boy named Tom and his dog Spot went to the beach. They liked to play in the sand and look for shells. Tom saw a big ship in the water. He wondered if it was a pirate ship.

"Spot, do you think there are pirates on that ship?" he asked his dog.

Spot barked and wagged his tail. He did not know what pirates were, but he liked to follow Tom.

Tom and Spot ran to the shore. They saw a man with a hat and a hook. He was rowing a small boat to the land. He looked angry and mean.

"Ahoy, matey!" the man shouted. "I am Captain Hook, the most feared pirate in the seven seas. Give me your treasure or suffer!"

Tom and Spot were scared. They did not have any treasure. They only had a bucket and a shovel.

"Please, Mr. Pirate, we don't have any treasure. We are just playing," Tom said.

"Playing? Ha! You are lying. You must have hidden your gold and jewels somewhere. I will find them and take them. And I will make you walk the plank!" Captain Hook said.

He grabbed Tom's bucket and shovel and threw them in his boat. He reached for Tom and Spot.

But then, something happened. A big wave came and knocked over Captain Hook's boat. His hat and hook fell into the water. He splashed and screamed.

"Help! Help! I can't swim! Save me!" he cried.

Tom and Spot saw that the pirate was not so scary. He was just a silly man who could not swim. They felt sorry for him.

"Come on, Spot. Let's help him," Tom said.

They ran to the water and pulled Captain Hook to the shore. They gave him his hat and hook back.

"Thank you, thank you. You are very kind. I am sorry for being so mean. I was just lonely and bored. I don't have any friends on my ship. Will you be my friends?" Captain Hook asked.

His mom smiled and said, "No, he is not sick. He is fine. He is just resting. Lions are very active at night, but they sleep a lot during the day. They are called nocturnal animals."

The boy nodded and said, "Oh, I see. He is a nocturnal animal. That is a big word. Can I say hello to him?"

His mom said, "Sure, you can say hello, but be careful. Don't get too close to the cage. He might wake up and roar."

Timmy knew what to do. He took the puppy to the animal shelter where they could help find his family. The puppy was so happy to be reunited with his family and Timmy felt proud for helping him. The moral of the story is that we should always help others when they are sad or in need.

Lily was sad at first, but then she realized that her mom was right. She needed to take care of her teeth and not eat too much candy. She learned that sometimes, we need to listen to our parents and make good choices.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, her friend Timmy came over to play. Timmy said, "Lily, I have an invitation for you. Do you want to come to my birthday party next week?"

Lily thought for a moment and said, "Yes, I want to come to your party!" Timmy was happy that Lily would be coming to his party.

As they were playing, Lily noticed that Timmy's room was very smelly. She suggested, "Timmy, maybe we can open a window to let some fresh air in. Your room smells bad."

Timmy agreed and they opened the window. The fresh air made the room smell much better. They continued to play and have fun together.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer named Tim. Tim had a big field where he grew lots of hay. He loved to tie the hay into big bales and stack them up high. 

One day, Tim's friend Tom came to visit. Tom was very competitive and loved to play games. He challenged Tim to a race to see who could tie the most hay bales in one hour. 

Tim and Tom worked very hard, tying and stacking the hay bales as fast as they could. They were both very competitive and didn't want to lose. In the end, they tied the same number of hay bales and both won the race. They were both very happy and proud of themselves.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the park with her friends. One day, as she was playing, she saw a big red ball. She was eager to play with it, so she ran towards it. Suddenly, she slipped on some mud and hurt her knee.

Her friend, Timmy, saw what happened and ran to her. "Are you okay, Lily?" he asked. "I'm okay," she said, "but my knee hurts." Timmy helped her up and they walked to a nearby bench to rest.

As they sat there, they saw some steam coming from a nearby manhole. "Look, Timmy!" Lily exclaimed. "It's like a little volcano!" Timmy smiled and said, "Yeah, it's pretty cool." Suddenly, they heard a loud noise and saw the manhole cover spring open. Hot steam shot out and burned them both. They cried out in pain and ran home to get help.

Lily's mom took them to the hospital, but their burns were too severe. They had to stay in the hospital for a long time and missed playing in the park. They learned to be careful around steam and manholes. The end.

Ellie felt happy and proud of herself for being able to help someone. She realized that even though she didn't fit in with the monkeys' game, she could still be a good friend and leader to others who needed her help.

Once upon a time, there was a little gray mouse named Max. Max lived in a cozy hole in the wall of a big house. One day, Max went to get a drink from the tap in the kitchen. But, when he turned the tap, no water came out! Max was very thirsty and didn't know what to do.

Suddenly, Max heard a loud noise coming from the other side of the kitchen. It was the cat, Fluffy! Fluffy was always trying to catch Max and eat him. Max was scared and didn't know how to get away from Fluffy. 

Just then, Max had an idea. He remembered that there was a piece of cheese in the cupboard that had started to rot. Max quickly ran to the cupboard, grabbed the cheese, and threw it at Fluffy. Fluffy was so distracted by the smelly cheese that Max was able to run away and hide in his cozy hole. Max was safe and happy, and he never forgot to check the tap before he got thirsty again.

He rode his bike towards Ben and Sam and tried to break their chain. He bumped into Ben's bike and made him fall. Ben hurt his knee and started to cry. Sam got angry and said, "Leave us alone, you meanie. You are not nice. Go away."

The big boy did not listen. He said, "No, I will not go away. I will take your bikes. They are mine now." He grabbed Sam's bike and tried to ride away. But he did not know that Sam's bike had a trick. Sam had tied a rope to his bike and to a tree. When the big boy rode too far, the rope pulled him back and made him spin. He lost his balance and crashed into the tree. He hurt his head and started to cry.

Ben and Sam ran to their bikes and tried to get away. But they were too late. The big boy's friends came to the park. They saw what happened and got angry. They said, "You two, you are in trouble. You hurt our friend. We will hurt you." They chased Ben and Sam and caught them. They kicked and punched them and took their bikes. They said, "These are our bikes now. You can never have them back."

Ben and Sam were very sad and scared. They had no bikes and no friends. They wished they had never met the big boy. They wished they had stayed home. They hugged each other and cried. They were loyal, but they were not happy. The end.

Tom and Anna liked to jog in the park with their dog, Rex. They jogged fast and slow, up and down, and around the trees. Rex ran with them and barked happily. They had fun and felt good.

One day, they saw a big cabinet in the park. It was brown and shiny, and had a door and a lock. Tom and Anna were curious. They wanted to see what was inside the cabinet. They ran to the cabinet and tried to open the door.

"Maybe there are toys or books or candy in there," Tom said.

"Or maybe there are monsters or spiders or snakes," Anna said.

They pulled and pushed, but the door did not open. They looked for a key, but they did not find one. They knocked and kicked, but no one answered.

"Let's go, Tom. This cabinet is boring and scary," Anna said.

But Tom did not listen. He wanted to open the door. He saw a big rock near the cabinet. He picked up the rock and threw it at the lock. He hoped the lock would break.

But the lock did not break. The rock bounced back and hit Tom in the head. Tom fell down and cried. He had a big bump and a lot of blood. Anna screamed and ran to Tom. She hugged him and called for help.

Rex barked and ran to the cabinet. He smelled something bad. He saw smoke and fire coming out of the cabinet. He heard a loud noise. He was scared and ran away.

The cabinet was not a cabinet. It was a bomb. Someone had put it in the park to hurt people. Tom and Anna did not know that. They were too young and too curious. They jogged to the wrong place at the wrong time. They made a big mistake. The end.

"Look, ice!" Tom says. "Can we go on it?"

Mia shakes her head. "No, Tom. Ice is not safe. It can break. We can fall in the water. The water is very cold. We can get sick."

Tom frowns. He wants to go on the ice. He thinks it looks fun. He sees some ducks on the ice. They are not cold. They are not sick.

"Look, ducks!" Tom says. "They are on the ice. They are fine. Why can't we?"

Mia sighs. She knows Tom is curious. She tries to explain. "Ducks are different, Tom. They have feathers. They have webbed feet. They can swim. They can fly. We are not ducks. We have skin. We have shoes. We can't swim. We can't fly. We are not safe on the ice."

Tom thinks for a moment. He understands. He does not want to get sick. He does not want to fall in the water. He does not want to be a duck. He wants to be a boy.

"Okay, Mia. You are right. Ice is not safe. We are not ducks. We are friends. Let's go make a snowman instead."

Mia smiles. She is happy. She likes to make snowmen. She likes to be friends with Tom. They hold hands and walk away from the lake. They look for a good spot to make a snowman. They have fun in the snow.

"Ben, help me get an apple!" Lily said.

Ben had a stick. He tried to poke an apple with the stick, but it was hard. He poked and poked, but the apple did not fall.

"Ben, you are not good at poking!" Lily said.

Ben felt sad. He did not like when Lily was mean to him. He threw the stick away and sat on the grass.

Lily saw that Ben was sad. She felt sorry for him. She wanted to make him happy again.

"Ben, I am sorry. You are good at poking. I was just hungry. Can we be friends again?" Lily said.

Ben looked at Lily. He saw that she was sorry. He smiled and nodded.

"OK, Lily. We can be friends again. But how can we get an apple?" Ben said.

Lily thought for a moment. She had an idea.

"Look, Ben! There is a ladder by the shed. We can use it to climb the tree and get an apple!" Lily said.

Ben liked the idea. He got up and ran to the shed. He brought the ladder to the tree. He helped Lily climb the ladder and reach an apple.

"Here, Ben! I got an apple for you!" Lily said.

She gave the apple to Ben. He took a big bite and smiled.

"Thank you, Lily! This is a yummy apple!" Ben said.

They shared the apple and ate it together. They were happy and calm. They hugged and said sorry again.

They learned that poking is not always the best way to get what you want. Sometimes, you need to use your brain and your heart. And sometimes, you need to say sorry and be kind.

"Sorry, Ben. I was wrong too. You can have the coconut. It is yours," Lily said.

Her friends agreed. They ran and hid behind the sofa, the table, the chair, and the curtain. Lily counted to ten. Then she said, "Freeze!"

She looked around. She saw Ben behind the sofa. He was still. She saw Mia behind the table. She was still. She saw Sam behind the chair. He was still. She saw Anna behind the curtain. She was still.

But she saw something else. She saw a black cat. It was on the window sill. It was not still. It was moving its tail. Lily said, "I see you, cat. You are out."

The cat looked at Lily. It did not understand. It meowed. It jumped off the window sill. It ran away.

Lily and her friends laughed. They said, "Silly cat. You can't play freeze. You are not a friend. You are a cat."

They played again. They had fun. They ate cake. They sang happy birthday. Lily was very happy. It was her best birthday ever.

Ben and Sam were brothers who liked to play outside. One day, they found a big stone on the hill. Ben had an idea. He said, "Let's roll the stone down the hill and see what happens." Sam nodded and they pushed the stone with all their might.

The stone rolled down the hill very fast. It made a loud noise and hit many things on the way. It hit a tree, a fence, a car, and a house. The people who owned the things were very angry and scared. They came out and shouted at Ben and Sam. "What have you done? You broke our things! You could have hurt someone! You are very bad boys!"

Ben and Sam felt sorry and scared. They did not mean to cause trouble. They ran away and hid behind a bush. They cried and hugged each other. They wished they had not rolled the stone down the hill.

A man came and found them. He was the owner of the house that the stone hit. He looked at them and said, "Why did you roll the stone down the hill? Did you not think of the consequences?" Ben and Sam said, "We are sorry, sir. We just wanted to have fun. We did not think of the consequences. We are very sorry."

The man said, "I understand that you are sorry, but sorry is not enough. You have to learn from your mistake and make up for it. You have to help me fix my house and the other things that you broke. You also have to apologize to the other people that you upset. Do you agree?" Ben and Sam nodded and said, "Yes, sir. We agree. We will help you and say sorry to the others. We will not roll stones down hills anymore. We will be more careful and thoughtful."

The man smiled and said, "That is good. I am glad that you are willing to take responsibility and learn from your mistake. Come on, let's go and start working. Maybe we can also have some fun along the way." Ben and Sam smiled and followed the man. They learned a valuable lesson that day. They learned that actions have consequences and that they should think before they act. They also learned that saying sorry is not enough and that they should make up for their wrongs. They also learned that being careful and thoughtful is better than being reckless and careless. They also learned that the man was kind and forgiving and that they could be friends with him. They never rolled stones down hills again.

Suddenly, his mom shouted "Tyler, don't even think of it!" He was shocked and ashamed, but his mom knew it was for his own good. 

She explained that eating black birds on a busy street was dangerous because the traffic could hurt him if he wasn't careful. Tyler felt sad and disappointed that he couldn't taste the black bird, but he also felt relieved that he was safe.

Although Tyler couldn't taste the black bird, he learned a valuable lesson: it's always important to stay safe even if you really want to do something.

Mia was sad and looked down. "I'm sorry," she said.

Mama took a deep breath and then knelt down to hug her daughter. "It's ok sweetheart," said Mama. "I forgive you."

Mia was so happy she smiled and hugged her mama tight.

That night, they ate dinner together. Mia had made a delicious dish. She had boiled the rice until it was soft, but the curry she added was too sour.

Mama tasted it, then smiled softly at her daughter. "Mia, I forgive you for making it too sour," she said.

Mia pushed the plate away, embarrassed. But Mama picked it back up and started to eat. "It's good! I can still eat it," she said.

Mama's act of forgiveness made Mia feel so happy. She smiled and vowed to always remember the lesson her mama had taught her that day.
